0 · Trial Book Front-Matter — Charge / Range / Venue / Elements per Count (cause-by-cause)

PURPOSE: This section is a counsel-facing trial-book skeleton. It compresses each active cause to (i) charge and statutory citation, (ii) statutory punishment range, (iii) venue and presiding court, (iv) elements the State must prove, (v) top-line affirmative defenses and pretrial motions to preserve. It is not a substitute for counsel's own charge-conference workup; it is a triage anchor so a reviewing lawyer with limited preparation hours can enter the file already oriented to the trial architecture. Every citation herein is drawn from Texas Penal Code, Texas Code of Criminal Procedure, and Texas Rules of Evidence as they read on the offense date; counsel to independently confirm current text before any charge conference.

0.1 · Travis County — Cause D-1-DC-25-303689

ChargeAssault Family Violence Impede Breath / Circulation — Texas Penal Code Section 22.01(b)(2)(B) (impeding normal breathing or circulation by applying pressure to throat or neck, or by blocking nose or mouth, of a person whose relationship with the actor is described by Texas Family Code Section 71.0021(b), 71.003, or 71.005).
GradeThird-degree felony as pleaded. Grand Jury Special Findings entered 2026-01-14 designating a pillow as a deadly weapon — if that special issue is submitted to the trial jury and found, elevates offense character to a Section 3g / Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 42A.054 offense for parole-eligibility purposes and triggers Texas Government Code Section 508.145(d) actual-time-served computation on the deadly-weapon finding.
Punishment rangeThird-degree felony: 2–10 years Texas Department of Criminal Justice / Institutional Division plus fine up to $10,000 (Texas Penal Code Section 12.34). Community supervision eligibility governed by Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 42A; jury-recommended community supervision is unavailable if a deadly-weapon Special Issue is found.
Venue / courtTravis County. District court of assignment on D-1-DC-25-303689 (Judge of record to be confirmed by Travis District Clerk).
Elements the State must prove(i) the defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly; (ii) caused bodily injury to another person; (iii) whose relationship with the defendant falls within Texas Family Code Sections 71.0021(b), 71.003, or 71.005; (iv) by intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly impeding the normal breathing or circulation of the blood of the person; (v) by applying pressure to the person's throat or neck or by blocking the person's nose or mouth. Deadly-weapon Special Issue: whether the defendant used or exhibited a deadly weapon (the pillow) during commission of the offense.
Affirmative defenses / pretrial preservationRecantation of the complaining witness (2025-11-08 written recantation to Travis County District Attorney; Section 5A Exhibits A–F). Speedy-trial preservation under the Sixth Amendment to the United States Constitution and Article I Section 10 of the Texas Constitution per Barker v. Wingo, 407 U.S. 514 (1972); Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.151 delay-release remedy where the State is not ready within 90 days for a felony. Confrontation Clause per Crawford v. Washington, 541 U.S. 36 (2004). Franks v. Delaware, 438 U.S. 154 (1978) challenge to any charging affidavit found to contain deliberate falsehood or reckless disregard. Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 38.371 statutory admissibility framework for family-violence cases (specific-relationship evidence admissible; force reciprocity). Michael Morton Act discovery under Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 39.14.

0.4 · Collin County — Cause 199-80977-2026

ChargeTampering with Governmental Record — Texas Penal Code Section 37.10(c)(2)(A) (as pleaded in the Collin 199th District Court indictment entered 2026-02-26).
GradeSecond-degree felony as pleaded under Section 37.10(c)(2)(A) — applies where the actor's intent is to defraud or harm another and the governmental record is one of the enumerated document classes.
Punishment rangeSecond-degree felony: 2–20 years Texas Department of Criminal Justice / Institutional Division plus fine up to $10,000 (Texas Penal Code Section 12.33).
Venue / court199th District Court, Collin County. Judge Angela Tucker presiding. Clerk of record: Mike Gould, Collin County District Clerk.
Elements the State must prove(i) the defendant made, presented, or used a governmental record; (ii) with knowledge of its falsity; (iii) with intent that it be taken as a genuine governmental record; and, for the (c)(2)(A) enhancement, (iv) with intent to defraud or harm another; (v) the record being one of the enumerated document types under Section 37.10(c)(2). Reviewing counsel to demand a bill of particulars identifying (a) the specific record, (b) the specific falsity, (c) the intent-to-defraud-or-harm theory, and (d) the enumerated document class relied on.
Affirmative defenses / pretrial preservationIdentity/authorship challenge (who executed the record). Knowledge-of-falsity challenge. Intent-to-defraud challenge. Enumerated-document-class challenge. Correct fallback ladder: Section 37.10(c)(2)(A) second-degree felony applies where both the enumerated-document class AND intent-to-defraud-or-harm are proven; if the document-class predicate fails but generic governmental-record tampering + intent to defraud/harm survives, the grade is a state-jail felony under Section 37.10(c)(1) (see Kirkpatrick v. State reflecting the statutory structure); Class A misdemeanor is the fallback ONLY if both the enumerated document class AND the intent-to-defraud-or-harm enhancement fail. Counsel to model plea calculus against all three rungs, not two. Franks challenge to charging affidavit. Michael Morton Act discovery.
Principal report (N440 2026-09-04)Identity-authorship counter-claim — specific named alleged forgers: Kyle asserts he did not execute the governmental record underlying the tampering charge. Kyle alleges Caitlyn Elizabeth Grant + her father (identity pending intake) are the actual actors who signed Kyle's signature on that record. Attaches names to the identity/authorship defense already anchored above. Requires: (a) bill of particulars identifying the specific document, date, and alleged victim; (b) certified indictment + probable-cause affidavit from Collin County District Clerk (Mike Gould) to confirm all parties named and identify the affiant / complaining witness; (c) forensic questioned-document examination of the alleged Kyle-signature against known-exemplar Kyle signatures. Charging posture per current record: Kyle Scott Harris is the sole named defendant on Collin cause 199-80977-2026; Caitlyn Grant is NOT named as co-defendant on this indictment. Forgery time-frame anchor (N440): Kyle asserts the alleged forgery by Caitlyn Grant + her father occurred BEFORE the 2025-08-25 Protective Order petition. Causation significance: reframes the Protective Order as potentially retaliatory or cover for prior forgery conduct rather than a defensive response to it. Exact-date anchor, instrument identification, and provenance of Kyle's knowledge required at intake.

0.5 · Underlying Collin Civil — Cause 429-55152-2025 (Grant v. Harris)

Matter typeCivil Protective Order under Texas Family Code Chapter 85 (as opposed to a Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.292 magistrate's emergency protective order). Pro se petition filed by Caitlyn Elizabeth Grant 2025-08-25; Ex Parte Temporary Protective Order granted same date.
Court429th District Court, Collin County.
Relevance to criminal filePredicate for any Section 25.07 violation charge (see Collin Cause 199-80678-2026). Any weakness in the underlying protective-order procedure (notice, service, hearing) may translate to a knowledge-of-order or validity challenge in the Section 25.072 case. Reviewing counsel to pull the entire 429-55152-2025 file (petition, ex parte order, service return, final hearing transcript if any) and evaluate whether a collateral attack on the protective order itself is viable or whether the challenge posture is limited to notice-and-knowledge.
Restraining Order vs Protective Order — legal distinctionA civil Temporary Restraining Order [TRO] under Texas Rule of Civil Procedure 680 is a civil injunction enforced by civil contempt only; violation is not a standalone crime. A Protective Order under Texas Family Code Chapter 85 is civilly issued but criminally enforced — violation is a Class A misdemeanor under Texas Penal Code Section 25.07, elevatable to third-degree felony on stacking predicates (prior conviction, assault-in-violation, stalking-in-violation). Caitlyn Grant's filing in Collin 429-55152-2025 is a Chapter 85 Protective Order, NOT a Rule 680 TRO. This is why the alleged violation in Collin 199-80678-2026 is a criminal (Section 25.07) matter rather than civil contempt. The two instruments are commonly conflated in lay usage but carry categorically different enforcement mechanics.
Principal report (N440 2026-09-04) — third-party influence + friendship claimThird-party influence theory: Kyle alleges Caitlyn Grant has been approached by unidentified third parties who are attempting to influence her to cooperate with them in prosecuting Kyle. If corroborated with identity, date, and act, this raises potential Texas Penal Code Section 36.05 (witness tampering) exposure against the approachers and generates Brady/Giglio impeachment material if any prosecution-team member is among them. Requires at intake: identities, dates, medium, offers/threats, whether Caitlyn accepted or refused, corroboration (screenshots, witnesses, recordings), and whether Caitlyn would testify to the approach. Friendship claim vs Protective Order contradiction: Kyle asserts Caitlyn Grant is his friend, which directly contradicts her 2025-08-25 pro se Protective Order petition. Two reconciliations to probe: (a) friendship was genuine and the Protective Order was procured through third-party influence or coercion (see above); (b) the relationship was mixed/volatile and "friend" is Kyle's characterization the record would not support. Requires at intake: nature and length of friendship, last friendly contact date, any post-Protective-Order communications reflecting friendship, and Kyle's explanation for why a friend would file a Chapter 85 Protective Order.

0.6 · Cross-Cutting Preservation Anchors (all causes)

  • Sixth Amendment speedy trial — preserve continuously per Barker v. Wingo, 407 U.S. 514 (1972). Article 32A.02 is dead law (Meshell v. State, 739 S.W.2d 246 (Tex. Crim. App. 1987); repealed Acts 2005, 79th Leg., Ch. 828); do not cite it.
  • Delay-release remedy — Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.151 (State not ready within 90 days on felony detainer — personal-bond release or bond reduction).
  • Michael Morton Act discovery — Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 39.14. Standing request in every cause; specific request for the 2025-11-08 Bobbi Jo Rice recantation email and any grand-jury materials in which that recantation was (or was not) presented.
  • Franks challenges — Franks v. Delaware, 438 U.S. 154 (1978). Pull every charging affidavit, arrest affidavit, and search-warrant affidavit; hunt for deliberate falsehood or reckless disregard for the truth by the affiant. Preserve early — Franks challenges are lost if not staged.
  • Confrontation Clause — Crawford v. Washington, 541 U.S. 36 (2004). Any testimonial hearsay by the complaining witness, if she does not appear at trial or takes the Fifth, is presumptively inadmissible.
  • Statement-of-recent-fabrication rehab — Texas Rule of Evidence 801(e)(1)(B). Anticipate a State motion to admit prior-consistent statements of the complaining witness to rehabilitate against the recantation impeachment. Timing predicate: Texas cases require the prior consistent statement to pre-date the alleged improper motive or influence being rebutted — counsel to build the pre-motive-timeline audit so any State-offered "prior consistent" is tested against that predicate rather than admitted as-of-right.
  • "Own the recantation" branch script — State's dominant single move. The State's strongest single attack is not expert-witness Battered Woman Syndrome [BWS] testimony; it is calling Ms. Rice on direct examination, having her expressly admit she wrote the recantation, and then having her testify that the recantation is false and the original allegation was true — drawing the sting on Texas Rule of Evidence 613(a) so extrinsic republication is blocked. Counsel must prepare two branch scripts: (a) ADMISSION branch — if Ms. Rice admits authorship of the recantation on direct, lock in the oral admission, do not attempt Rule 613(a) extrinsic republication (the rule blocks it once admitted), and pivot to Ms. Rice's explanation for the recantation — that explanation is the actual credibility battlefield, tested against every pre-November-8 contemporaneous contact chronology, financial-arrangement absence, and independent corroboration. (b) DENIAL branch — if Ms. Rice denies authorship or content, execute the full Rule 613(a) predicate (time, place, person), lay Beth Martin native-device authentication under Rule 901, and offer the segregated inconsistent portion; simultaneously stack Rule 801(e)(1)(B) prior-consistent rehabilitation counters against the State's original-statement-as-prior-consistent play by demonstrating pressure/motive at the moment of the original statement (injury moment, officer prompt, fear).
  • USMC mitigation posture (bond + sentencing) — the Principal is a United States Marine Corps Gunnery Sergeant / Marine Raider / Scout Sniper. This is bond-hearing and sentencing mitigation architecture: length of honorable service, combat deployments, chain-of-command references, medical / traumatic-brain-injury / post-traumatic-stress workup, and Veterans Treatment Court eligibility screening. Reviewing counsel to develop this thread pretrial — not day-of-sentencing.

1 · Executive Summary

Kyle Scott Harris, a Texas resident, is a pretrial detainee in the custody of the Travis County Sheriff's Office at the Travis County Correctional Complex on Travis County cause number D-1-DC-25-303689 (first-degree felony with a Grand Jury deadly-weapon Special Finding entered 2026-01-14 naming a pillow as the deadly weapon), with parallel misdemeanor causes C-1-CR-25-502783 and C-1-CR-25-502784 pending in Travis County and parallel Collin County matters 199-80678-2026 (Violation of Bond / Protective Order 2+ Times, 199th District Court, Judge Angela Tucker) and 199-80977-2026 (Tampering with Governmental Record, 199th District Court, Judge Angela Tucker), together with the underlying civil protective-order matter 429-55152-2025 (Grant v. Harris, 429th District Court) and the same-day magistration record DCMAG-49928-2025 (Judge Lisa Bronchetti). The complaining witness on the Travis County matters is Bobbi Jo Rice; on 2025-11-08 (sixteen days after the Travis warrant issued) Ms. Rice sent an email to the Travis County District Attorney's Office stating in her own words that the alleged incident “never happened,” and in a subsequent SMS thread to the Principal's mother Beth Martin she offered in writing to “testify on his behalf to his innocence” — both preserved in the seven-screenshot exhibit set covered in Section 5A. During Kyle's custody, two dogs owned by Kyle — Gunner (living) and Nebula (deceased) — were taken by Collin County Animal Services under a purported surrender form allegedly bearing the signature of Bobbi Jo Rice; Kyle asserts he never authorized Ms. Rice or any other person to sign a surrender on his behalf, never surrendered ownership of either dog, and never consented to euthanasia of Nebula. Nebula was euthanized while in Collin County Animal Services custody; Gunner was adopted out to an unknown third party. Kyle's appointed defense counsel are Chris Holub (Travis) and John B. “Brad” Setterberg, Texas Bar Number 24043915 (Collin, Letter of Representation filed 2026-03-27). This dossier consolidates the factual record, the identified actors, the laws and constitutional rights potentially implicated, the evidence anchors in hand and the evidence still needed, the complaints and escalation packages already drafted and staged for delivery, and the library of Principal-signable instruments available for counsel to review, adapt, and deploy at counsel's discretion.

Legal characterization: Under Texas law, dogs are personal property (chattel). The Texas Supreme Court in Strickland v. Medlen, 397 S.W.3d 184 (Tex. 2013), held that Texas law does not recognize sentimental / companion-animal / intrinsic-value damages for the loss of a dog — only fair market value or, where market value is not readily determinable, the “special or pecuniary” value based on utility to the owner. Prior versions of this dossier that cited Bueckner v. Hamel, 886 S.W.2d 368 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 1994, writ denied) as authority for sentimental-value recovery are retracted; Strickland v. Medlen is the controlling authority. Continuous title extinguishes third-party good-faith-purchaser defense on receipt of the Ownership Declaration and Reclamation Demand.

5A.3 · Impeachment + Admissibility Framework Citations (rewritten 2026-09-03)

  • Texas Rules of Evidence 613(a) — Prior inconsistent statement of a witness. If the witness testifies, opposing counsel must confront the witness with the statement and give the witness opportunity to explain or deny before offering extrinsic evidence. SMS thread predicate satisfies cleanly on this rule.
  • Texas Rules of Evidence 607 — Any party may impeach any witness (including one it called). No voucher rule in Texas.
  • Texas Rules of Evidence 803(3) — Statement of the declarant's then-existing state of mind, emotion, or intent. Rice statements bearing on her contemporaneous intent to testify, her contemporaneous perception of the Principal, or her contemporaneous premises-control conduct are admissible substantively under this exception.
  • Texas Rules of Evidence 807 — Residual hearsay exception. Reserved for substantive use of Rice's recantation statements if she becomes unavailable at trial; requires notice, guarantees of trustworthiness, and no other exception fits — counsel to build the Rule 807 predicate independently.
  • Forfeiture-by-wrongdoing — Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 38.49 (NOT Rule 803 or Rule 804(b)(6)). Texas's operative statutory framework for forfeiture-by-wrongdoing admission of otherwise-inadmissible hearsay from an unavailable witness is Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 38.49 — the Federal Rule 804(b)(6) analogue and any Texas Rule 803(a) framing are inapposite. The State must establish, outside the presence of the jury by preponderance of the evidence, that the accused engaged in, directed, or acquiesced in wrongdoing that was intended to procure and did in fact procure the witness's unavailability. The wrongful act need not itself be criminal, and preventing testimony need not be the sole motive, but causation and purpose still matter (see Brown v. State, holding that attenuated or speculative causation is insufficient). State-side scenario map: mother-side or Attorney-in-Fact-side contact does NOT automatically become Principal forfeiture — the State must tie the Principal through direction, agreement, or acquiescence AND causation of unavailability. Ms. Rice's actual appearance at trial defeats forfeiture entirely. See also the DPOA scope-warning at Q8.04 — execution of an unrestricted Durable Power of Attorney formalizes agency in a manner that materially strengthens the State's Art. 38.49 attribution posture under Rule 801(e)(2)(C) and 801(e)(2)(D).
  • Texas Rules of Evidence 801(d) — Not offered for truth. Certain Rice statements (e.g., verbal acts evidencing unauthorized disposition of Principal's property) are non-hearsay because they are offered to prove the fact of the utterance, not its truth.
  • Texas Rules of Evidence 106 + 107 — Rule of Optional Completeness. If the defense introduces portions of the SMS thread, the State may introduce related portions necessary to make the introduced portions understood. Counsel must sequence and select exhibits with Rule 107 exposure in mind.
  • Texas Rules of Evidence 901 — Authentication foundation for the SMS thread: sponsoring witness (Beth Martin, custodian of the receiving device) plus forensic device-extraction report (Cellebrite / GrayKey / iTunes-Finder unencrypted backup extract) plus SMS-record subpoena to Ms. Rice's carrier for message-identifier / SS7-log corroboration.
  • Texas Rules of Evidence 401 / 402 / 403 — Relevance and Rule 403 balancing. Every proposed exhibit must clear a Rule 403 balancing where cumulative, marginally probative, or collateral matter risks exclusion.
  • Texas Rules of Evidence 608(a) + 608(b) — Character for truthfulness. Rule 608(b) prohibits extrinsic proof of specific instances of conduct offered to attack character for truthfulness; such specific instances may only be inquired into on cross. Counsel must not stage witness impeachment through collateral extrinsic proof.
  • Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 39.14 (Michael Morton Act) — Prosecution must disclose any statement of a witness that is material, including exculpatory recantations.
  • Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 38.371 — Evidence of the nature of the relationship between the actor and the complainant in a family-violence prosecution; potentially cuts both ways and requires Rule 403 balancing.
  • Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 38.22 — Statements of the accused: predicate for suppression of any un-Mirandized custodial statement.
  • Sixth Amendment Confrontation Clause · Crawford v. Washington, 541 U.S. 36 (2004) — Testimonial hearsay is barred unless the declarant is unavailable and the defendant had a prior opportunity to cross-examine. Rice's prior statements to law enforcement are testimonial; the State may not offer them as substantive evidence if Rice does not testify and the defense had no prior cross opportunity.
  • Brady v. Maryland, 373 U.S. 83 (1963) — Suppression of favorable evidence material to guilt violates due process.
  • Giglio v. United States, 405 U.S. 150 (1972) — Extends Brady to impeachment evidence.
  • Kyles v. Whitley, 514 U.S. 419 (1995) — Prosecution's duty extends to evidence known only to police / investigators.
  • Napue v. Illinois, 360 U.S. 264 (1959) — Prosecution may not knowingly allow false testimony to stand uncorrected.
  • Willover v. State, 70 S.W.3d 841 (Tex. Crim. App. 2002) — In a criminal case the State is the party-opponent; the complaining witness's prior statements are NOT party-opponent admissions under Tex. R. Evid. 801(e)(2). Prior versions of this section that cited Rule 801(e)(2) as the admissibility basis for Rice statements against the State's position are retracted.

7A.2 · Cross-Cutting Notes for Reviewing Counsel

  • Prison Litigation Reform Act exhaustion. For § 1983 jail-conditions lanes — exhaust internal grievances first.
  • In Forma Pauperis. File § 1983 complaints in Western District of Texas (Austin Division) with 28 U.S.C. § 1915 application.
  • Sovereign-immunity ceilings. Texas Tort Claims Act caps state-law claims against governmental units at $100,000 / $300,000 (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 101.023). Federal § 1983 has no cap.
  • Qualified immunity. Individual officer defendants will assert. Overcome by clearly-established showing. Thompson v. Clark (2022) made post-2022 malicious-prosecution law clearly established.
  • Statutes of limitations. Texas 1-year for malicious prosecution and defamation (§ 16.002(a)). Texas 2-year for personal injury and § 1983 (Owens v. Okure). § 1986 = 1-year. Civil RICO = 4-year from discovery. Malicious-prosecution clock accrues at favorable termination. File within one week of favorable termination to lock the 1-year windows.
  • Order of operations. Win the criminal case first. Heck v. Humphrey (512 U.S. 477) bars claims that would necessarily imply invalidity of an outstanding conviction.
  • Contingency posture. Ranks 1–10 fee-shifting under § 1988. Ranks 11–18 fee-shifting under respective statutes. Ranks 19–42 standard plaintiffs' contingency (33–40%).
  • Ladder disclaimer. Dollar estimates are single-figure midpoints. Actual recovery depends on venue, jury pool, defendant solvency, sovereign-immunity ceilings, qualified-immunity rulings, contingency-fee take, settlement dynamics, and case-specific proof developed in discovery.

15.6 · Staggered Outreach Sequence (probability-first, not parallel-blast)

Positioning line for every pitch (not the story you send — the frame you write to). Kyle's strongest media proposition is NOT “A man says Travis County is corrupt” — thousands of pitches look like that. The pitchable frame is:

“An incarcerated Texas defendant says the documentary record across two counties reveals potentially contradictory proceedings, prolonged pretrial detention, disputed evidentiary foundations, alleged failures of counsel and discovery, and alleged obstruction inside the jail — and his family has assembled the docket numbers, filings, records requests, timelines and source documents necessary for an independent reporter to test every claim.”

That is an investigative proposition, not a grievance. Every pitch subject line and cover paragraph writes toward that frame.

Sequenced fire order (do NOT blast 100 journalists at once). Serious investigative desks compare notes; parallel-blast pitches get triaged out as low-quality mail. Stagger:

  1. Wave 1 — Colloff. Highest documented subject fit + Austin-based + records-heavy investigative track. Give her a real window (~5 business days) before firing next wave.

16 · Theory of the Case — 8 Perspectives (Record-Over-Character Discipline Lock)

Discipline lock — anchor every perspective to records, not to complainant character

Principle. Defense theory does not turn on whether the jury finds the complaining witness sympathetic or unsympathetic. Defense theory turns on what she said, to whom, when, and what independently authenticated documents memorialize it. The stronger defense architecture reduces dependence on complainant credibility wherever possible and rests instead on: original SMS content authenticated under Texas Rules of Evidence 901; the purported 2025-11-08 email to the Travis County District Attorney's Office; prosecution records showing whether it was received, triaged, and transmitted to defense; prior sworn statements; timestamps; officer body-worn-camera and interview recordings; and objective documentary contradictions.

Why this discipline matters. A defense that turns on complainant-character attack collapses into a character trial and hands the State a rehabilitation opening. A defense that turns on record-based contradiction survives even where the complainant later takes the stand in a State-friendly posture. The defense pre-commits to the second architecture.

“The jury does not have to decide whether the complaining witness is a good person or a bad person. The jury has to decide what she said, when she said it, and what the contemporaneous records prove.”

Section-wide discipline. Every one of the 8 perspectives below is written to that lock — anchor to records, not character. Where a perspective depends on witness credibility rather than documentary corroboration, the weakness is named explicitly in the “Strongest cross-cutting weakness” row.

16.1 · Perspective 1 — State / Prosecution Theory

Statement of the theory.Kyle committed a third-degree felony Assault Family Violence Impede Breath / Circulation under Texas Penal Code § 22.01(b)(2)(B) against Rice on or about 2025-09-06 (Cause D-1-DC-25-303689), with a Grand Jury deadly-weapon Special Finding (pillow) entered 2026-01-14 that carries Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 42A.054 community-supervision and Tex. Gov. Code § 508.145(d) parole-eligibility consequences, plus companion Class A misdemeanors (Terroristic Threat C-1-CR-25-502783, Unlawful Restraint C-1-CR-25-502784) and Collin County offenses (protective-order violation 199-80678-2026, tampering with a governmental record 199-80977-2026) sufficient to sustain the pretrial custody posture. Grade to be confirmed against certified indictment before any charge conference — dossier notes an internal instability with an earlier draft describing this cause as second-degree Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon under § 22.02, which would require a separately-pleaded § 22.02 count in the certified indictment. Travis and Collin district attorney's offices carry the burden. Required evidentiary spine.Rice's charging statements admissible and unimpeached · probable-cause affidavit accurate and unrebutted · deadly-weapon finding physically plausible · protective-order service and violation-conduct provable · witness-tampering conduct provable independent of Kyle's response to charges. Strongest supporting record citation.Travis D-1-DC-25-303689 grand-jury deadly-weapon finding (2026-01-14) · Collin causes 199-80678-2026 and 199-80977-2026 (indictments 2026-02-12 / 2026-02-26). The complaining witness communicated to the prosecuting office that the underlying event did not occur and offered to testify to his innocence. The custodial and charging posture cannot survive prompt Brady / Michael Morton disclosure, effective assistance of counsel, and a meaningful Speedy Trial demand. Wingo / Doggett) · Brady / Michael Morton motion · §7A civil-ladder Peeler-tolled malpractice preservation.

16.3 · Perspective 3 — Complaining-Witness (Rice) Theory at Charging

Statement of the theory.The narrative Rice's sworn or charging-instrument statements had to support to trigger the arrest, indictment, and pretrial custody — reconstructed from the record as it stood at charging, not as it stood after 2025-11-08. Required evidentiary spine.Rice's complaint / sworn statement content and date · investigating officer's incorporation of Rice's statements into probable-cause affidavit · grand-jury presentation content re: Rice statements · consistency of Rice statements across officer interview, magistration, and grand jury. Strongest supporting record citation.Placeholder pending discovery production: complaint affidavits, PC affidavits, grand-jury exhibit list. This perspective is the empty-frame Rice was placed into by charging; its content is discoverable, not assumed. Strongest cross-cutting weakness.record-over-character discipline lock applies here first. Any temptation to attack Rice's character rather than her documentary trail collapses this perspective into a character trial and hands the State a rehabilitation opening. The perspective is analyzed to understand what the State built, NOT to demolish Rice as a human being. Activates.Discovery motions (§16.1) · §5A contradictions table cross-reference · §5A cross-examination stack (blocks A–H) — but each block written to documentary contradiction, not to character.

16.4 · Perspective 4 — Recantation Theory (Rice's Actual Post-Charging Position)

Statement of the theory.On 2025-11-08 Rice wrote to the Travis County District Attorney's Office stating the underlying event did not occur, and subsequently offered to testify to Kyle's innocence. The recantation is not a defense narrative — it is a documentary event with a date, a sender, a recipient, and a memorialized chain-of-communication to third parties. Required evidentiary spine.Production and authentication of the 2025-11-08 email itself (Brady / Michael Morton mandate) · DA-office ingest / triage / response records · corroborating SMS to Beth Martin (§5A Exhibits A–F) · timeline anchor to 2025-11-26+ testify offer · treatment of the recantation in subsequent charging decisions (or absence of treatment, which itself is evidence). Strongest supporting record citation.ENVELOPE 3 pp. 3–9 verbatim SMS exhibits · §5A contradictions table · timing chronology entry 2025-11-08. Strongest cross-cutting weakness.Recantation witnesses are impeachable through the same character-attack-in-reverse mechanic in reverse — the State can attack Rice's post-recantation credibility as easily as the defense could have attacked her charging-era credibility. Corroboration > credibility. Independent documents matter more than Rice's in-court demeanor. Activates.Motion to Compel production of the 2025-11-08 email · Napue / Giglio disclosure motion · Motion in limine on prior inconsistent statements · §5A cross-exam stack · §16.8 systemic theory (State response or non-response to the recantation is a systemic-conduct data point).

Statement of the theory.Arrest and post-arrest processing were conducted lawfully — probable-cause affidavit accurate, arrest warrant validly issued, magistration compliant, custodial handling within Fourth and Fourteenth Amendment norms, and inter-agency handoff (US Marshals → Collin → Travis) documented and defensible. Delaware veracity audit of affidavit · magistration record from Judge Bronchetti (DCMAG-49928-2025, 2025-09-09) · TCCC transfer paperwork (2025-11-10) · jail-conditions record and grievance logs during pretrial custody. 16.7 · Perspective 7 — Civil-Liability Theory (the §7A ladder viewed as a coherent case, not a menu)

Statement of the theory.The 42-lane civil-recovery ladder (§7A) is not a menu of alternative claims — it is three coherent spines. (a) 42 U.S.C. §1983 Monell + Franks + Napue / Giglio spine against public actors. (b) Texas Civil Practice & Remedies Code Chapter 134 + Strickland v. Medlen, 397 S.W.3d 184 (Tex. 2013) + Texas Penal Code §42.092 spine against private actors regarding Gunner and Nebula (prior Bueckner v. Hamel citation superseded). (c) Peeler-doctrine-tolled legal-malpractice spine against Holub and Setterberg preserved contingent on outcome of the underlying criminal cause. Required evidentiary spine.§1983: exoneration or Heck bar cleared · Franks affidavit-veracity showing · Napue / Giglio suppression showing. Chapter 134: theft-liability elements + treble damages calculation. Strickland v. Medlen: chattel valuation framework (fair market value or special/pecuniary value; NO sentimental value recovery for a dog) for Gunner and Nebula. Peeler: underlying criminal cause resolved with prejudice to Kyle's liberty ceasing. Strongest supporting record citation.§7A 42-lane ladder + itemized property-loss schedule ($82,500–$405,000 subtotal) + aggregate exposure range $14.5M–$25M · §5A Rice contradictions table · §16.5 arresting-agency Franks inquiry. Strongest cross-cutting weakness.Order of operations discipline (red-box in §7A): “Win the criminal case first.” Prematurely filed civil claims risk Heck bar, adverse depositions, and factual lock-ins that damage the criminal defense (§16.2). Civil ladder is preservation-and-tolling posture until criminal cause resolves. Activates.All §7A instruments · preservation letters (Instruments 16 + 17) · declarations of ownership (Instruments 13 + 14) · rescission of purported surrender (Instrument 18) · State Bar grievances against Holub and Setterberg on Peeler-tolled preservation basis.

16.8 · Perspective 8 — Systemic / Pattern-and-Practice Theory (the frame that unifies 16.1–16.7)

Statement of the theory.Kyle's matter is not an isolated event. It is a data point in a systemic pattern that includes: (a) charging-continued-after-recantation posture, (b) indigent-defense adequacy in Travis and Collin counties, (c) magistration and bond posture under supervisory review, (d) jail-conditions and access-to-courts patterns at Travis County Correctional Complex, (e) cross-county coordination between Collin, Travis, and Melissa jurisdictions, (f) media / oversight body responsiveness. Required evidentiary spine.Kyle's record as anchor + comparator cases surfaced via records requests (§16.1 Michael Morton, §10 State Bar and Judicial Conduct filings) + independent investigative reporting (§15 Media Targets) + institutional-review filings (FBI civil rights, Texas Rangers, DSHS zoonosis, Innocence Project of Texas — §15.8). Strongest supporting record citation.§10 Complaint + Escalation Register · §15 Media Targets with staggered outreach + MEDIA EVIDENCE DOSSIER spec (§15.10) · §14 File Index · the ENVELOPE 3 42-lane civil ladder as a mapping of the systemic surface area. Strongest cross-cutting weakness.Systemic theories fail when the anchor case is contested or unresolved. Kyle's matter must reach a defensible resolution posture (dismissal, acquittal, non-adverse plea, or documented exoneration) before systemic claims carry to a general audience without prejudicing the anchor. The §15.9 “documents first, spokesperson second, Kyle last” architecture is the operating discipline for this perspective. Activates.Every prior perspective's instruments PLUS: FBI civil-rights referral · Texas Rangers escalation · State Bar Texas grievances · State Commission on Judicial Conduct complaint · Collin DA special-prosecutor package · Innocence Project of Texas intake · MEDIA EVIDENCE DOSSIER build on GO.

17.D · Locked Doctrine + Strategy Anchors (operator locks 2026-07-18 forward)

17.D.1 · Speedy Trial + Faretta Pro Se Election (rewritten 2026-09-03 to remove reliance on repealed statute)

Doctrine (corrected): Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 32A.02 (the “Speedy Trial Act”) was held unconstitutional in Meshell v. State, 739 S.W.2d 246 (Tex. Crim. App. 1987) and was subsequently repealed by the Texas Legislature (Acts 2005, 79th Leg., Ch. 828). Any prior version of this dossier that anchored a “90-day / 180-day statutory clock” on Article 32A.02 is retracted as citation to dead law. The live speedy-trial architecture for the Principal is: (a) Sixth Amendment to the United States Constitution as construed in Barker v. Wingo, 407 U.S. 514 (1972) — four-factor balancing (length of delay, reason for delay, defendant's assertion of the right, prejudice to the defendant); (b) Texas Constitution Article I, Section 10; (c) Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.151 (release from custody on personal bond or reduced bail where the State is not ready for trial within 90 days after commencement of detention for a felony). Pro se election under Faretta v. California, 422 U.S. 806 (1975) remains preserved as a strategic option pending retention decision from §16A Attorney Candidate Register — not as a default posture.

17.D.2 · Franks v. Delaware GHOST DOCKET Motion (12-day ghost-docket rush theory)

Doctrine: Franks v. Delaware, 438 U.S. 154 (1978) permits a defendant to challenge the veracity of a warrant affidavit and, on a substantial preliminary showing, obtain a hearing. The “GHOST DOCKET” theory in this case is that the 12-day interval between the alleged 2025-09-06 incident and the 2025-09-18 initial docket movement (with subsequent 2025-10-23 warrant issuance) is inconsistent with a genuine victim-driven felony complaint and consistent instead with an after-the-fact docket construction. Motion candidate to be developed with retained counsel from the §16A bench.

17.D.3 · Bond ≠ Warrant ≠ Charge Doctrine

Doctrine: Three separate instruments, each requiring a separate disposition. A discharged bond (Collin 202515270 discharged 2026-02-24) does not recall the warrant. A recalled warrant (Collin W202515270 recalled 2026-03-16) does not vacate the underlying charge. A vacated charge does not restore forfeited bond premium. Reviewing counsel must confirm the status of each instrument independently on each cause number; a settlement or dismissal on one instrument does not carry over automatically to the other two.

17.D.4 · Consolidated Pretrial Motion Package (rewritten 2026-09-03 — Greek framing stripped)

Doctrine: Where the calendar and case posture support it, retained counsel may elect to file the pretrial motion package as a single-day consolidated set rather than sequentially, so that opposing counsel and the trial court receive the full defense architecture in one docket entry. Candidate motion inventory (all subject to counsel selection, ordering, and revision): Core motions — speedy-trial demand under the Sixth Amendment / Barker v. Wingo / Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.151; Brady / Napue / Giglio / Kyles disclosure and Michael Morton Act Article 39.14 discovery demand; subpoena duces tecum to the Travis County District Attorney's Office for the 2025-11-08 Rice recantation communication and any related work product; motion in limine on prior-inconsistent-statement impeachment posture for the complaining witness under Texas Rules of Evidence 613; motion to quash the deadly-weapon Special Finding on the ground that the 2025-11-08 recantation was not presented to the grand jury (Article 39.14 predicate); Franks v. Delaware hearing motion challenging the veracity of the charging affidavit(s); motion to compel proffer memoranda; motion to sever if severance is warranted on Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 21.24 grounds; motion for pretrial evidentiary hearing under Texas Rules of Evidence 104; motion for expert-witness funds pursuant to Ake v. Oklahoma, 470 U.S. 68 (1985) if indigency supports; motion to disclose grand-jury minutes as Franks foundation; motion for change of venue if pretrial publicity supports; motion for individual voir dire on the family-violence panel. Pressure motions — motion to recuse if judicial-bias record supports; motion to reopen bond hearing on new-evidence or Article 17.151 grounds; motion for jail-conditions relief; motion for expedited docket call; motion to compel election if duplicative charges create a multiplicity problem. The final inventory, sequencing, and legal theory of each motion is a decision reserved to retained counsel.

17.D.5 · Witness Guardrail (operator lock)

Doctrine: No direct contact by the Principal, the Attorney-in-Fact, Beth Martin, or any family member with any complainant (Bobbi Jo Rice, Caitlyn Grant), any prosecutor, any judge, any opposing counsel, or any witness. All contact routes exclusively through licensed counsel or through a licensed investigator retained by counsel. Rationale: (i) Texas Penal Code Section 36.05 tampering-with-witness exposure, (ii) preservation of Section 5A recantation trail evidentiary value (spontaneous / non-coached statement value collapses on any post-recantation defense-side outreach), (iii) any active bond condition prohibiting contact.

17.D.6 · Bail Posture (rewritten 2026-09-03 — prior “Custody-as-Leverage” theory retracted)

Doctrine (corrected): The prior version of §17.D.6 asserted a “Custody-as-Leverage” theory premised on Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 32A.02 accelerating in the Principal's favor while in custody. Because Article 32A.02 is repealed dead law (see §17.D.1), that leverage does not exist. The live bail-and-release framework is: (a) Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.15 (factors governing the amount of bail: sufficient to give reasonable assurance of appearance, not oppressive, nature and circumstances of the offense, ability to make bail, future safety of victim and community); (b) Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.151 (statutory release-on-personal-bond-or-reduced-bail where the State is not ready for trial within 90 days after commencement of detention for a felony — a live trigger the defense should track and assert if the calendar supports it); (c) Sixth Amendment / Barker v. Wingo constitutional speedy-trial posture (§17.D.1). Any bond-out decision is a Principal + retained-counsel decision and is not to be framed as a “strategic” reason to remain in custody.

17.D.7 · Work-Product Protection for Dossier Custodian Materials

Doctrine: Materials prepared by Dossier Custodian (Troy DanDurand) in anticipation of the Principal's defense, at the Principal's direction and under the Statutory Durable Power of Attorney, are asserted as work-product under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(b)(3) and Texas Rule of Civil Procedure 192.5 (party / consultant / agent categories). This assertion is preserved for any subpoena, discovery request, or civil-side deposition targeting the dossier itself, the underlying research notes, or the custodian's process.

17.D.8 · Bail-Factors + Community-Supervision-Eligibility + Parole-Consequence Citation Stack (rewritten 2026-09-03)

Doctrine (corrected): The prior version of §17.D.8 misdescribed Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.152 as a generic family-violence bail-conditions statute. Article 17.152 in fact governs the DENIAL of bail (or specific conditions) upon a subsequent violation of a Texas Penal Code § 25.07 protective-order-violation charge — it is not the generic family-violence-with-deadly-weapon bail statute. The correct citation stack is: (a) Bail amount and factors: Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.15 (statutory factors); Article 17.151 (release trigger where State is not trial-ready within 90 days after felony detention commencement). (b) Firearm-surrender and protective-order bail conditions: Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 17.292 (magistrate emergency protective orders) and Texas Family Code Chapter 85 (protective orders) — not Article 17.152. (c) Community-supervision (probation) eligibility on Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon (D-1-DC-25-303689): Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 42A.054 lists offenses ineligible for judge-ordered community supervision, and Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon with an affirmative deadly-weapon finding falls within that exclusion — jury-recommended community supervision under Article 42A.055 remains available, subject to jury findings. (d) Parole-eligibility consequence of an affirmative deadly-weapon finding: Texas Government Code § 508.145(d) — NOT Article 42A.054 — is the statute that requires the Principal to serve one-half of the sentence (with day-for-day flat time for a portion) before parole eligibility, if an affirmative deadly-weapon finding is entered and sustained. Reviewing counsel must plan trial and punishment-phase strategy around each of these constraints separately, at the earliest pretrial posture.

17.D.9 · Tone Discipline (rewritten 2026-09-03 — branded triad stripped)

Doctrine: Every defense-side filing carries three characteristics: (a) precise and citation-grade — every factual assertion supported by a record citation, every legal proposition supported by a statute or case citation with pin cite; (b) restrained in tone — no rhetorical excess, no character attacks, no colloquialisms, no branded language; (c) durable — drafted to survive as a preservation record on any appellate posture whether the Principal is convicted, acquitted, or the charges are dismissed.

17.D.10 · Record-Only Defense (rewritten 2026-09-03 — Greek framing stripped)

Doctrine: The defense stands on facts, statutes, cases, and documentary evidence only. No smear of the complainants. No character attacks on the prosecution. No media grandstanding. The complainant impeachment in Section 5A rests entirely on the complainant's own written words as authenticated under Texas Rules of Evidence 901 and offered under Texas Rules of Evidence 613 (prior inconsistent statement) — not on defense-side narrative construction. This is a pre-commitment to a defense architecture that survives judicial scrutiny at every level of appellate review.

17.E · What §17 is NOT

Section 17 is not a strategy binding on reviewing counsel. It is a consolidation of intel that was previously scattered across three case-portal HTML files. Reviewing counsel is free to accept, modify, or reject any doctrine anchor listed in §17.D. Every cause number, bond number, warrant number, and dollar-range figure requires independent verification against the primary docket records (Travis County District Clerk / Collin County District Clerk / Collin County Bond Clerk) before use in any filing. Reviewing counsel's independent verification is the trial-admissible record; §17 is a briefing shortcut, not a substitute for that verification.

Confidential defense-preparation material prepared by a non-attorney friend of the Principal at the Principal's direction. Not legal advice. Privilege and work-product status not represented and to be determined by retained counsel. Every cause number, statute citation, case citation, and factual assertion in this dossier requires independent verification against primary docket and reporter sources before use in any filing.

Purpose of This Ledger

This document is a live running tally of every civil cause of action that may arise from the events underlying the criminal cases pending against Kyle Scott Harris in Travis County, Texas, and Collin County, Texas. It is a working attorney-work-product research file, updated as facts develop, as the criminal cases resolve, and as statutes of limitations run.

The purpose is threefold. First, to preserve every viable claim by tracking the applicable statute of limitations against each defendant and each theory. Second, to identify which claims are ripe now, which are conditional on the criminal outcome, and which are post-acquittal or post-dismissal only. Third, to give retained civil counsel a single instrument from which to draft complaints when the moment comes.

Every entry cites primary authority. Every entry names a defendant. Every entry ties to a factual predicate already documented in this Dossier. Nothing is speculative; every claim is anchored in facts that either are on the public record or are captured in complainant, victim, or eyewitness statements already in the file.

Legend

Priority Tier
A — Fire first. Facts are on the record now, statute of limitations is short, or defendant is a governmental entity with pre-suit notice deadlines.
B — Fire early. Facts are on the record now, no notice-of-claim deadline, but early filing preserves discovery leverage.
C — Fire on ripeness. Cause of action does not accrue until the criminal case resolves favorably (malicious prosecution, false imprisonment where predicate charge must terminate in Kyle's favor).
D — Investigate first. Facts partially known; requires records requests, deposition, or expert opinion before drafting.
Ripeness Codes
LIVE — Cause of action has accrued. Statute of limitations is running. File-ready subject to counsel review.
CONDITIONAL — Cause of action accrues on a triggering event (criminal case resolution, exhaustion of criminal appeals, notice-of-claim response).
POST-RESOLUTION — Cause of action cannot accrue until Kyle's criminal cases terminate favorably (dismissal, acquittal, or reversal on the merits).
INVESTIGATE — Facts under development. Ripeness not yet determinable.

Notice-of-Claim Alert

The Texas Tort Claims Act notice requirement is jurisdictional. A late or defective notice bars the state-law claim entirely — the governmental defendant will move to dismiss under Rule 91a or plea to the jurisdiction and will win. Federal § 1983 claims do not require pre-suit notice; those clocks run independently.

Complainant is instructed to draft, send by certified mail with return-receipt requested, and retain proof of service for each notice named above immediately. Retain civil counsel of record to sign the notices where practical.

Peeler Doctrine — Why Malpractice Waits

Under Peeler v. Hughes & Luce, 909 S.W.2d 494 (Tex. 1995), a criminal-defendant plaintiff cannot maintain a legal-malpractice action against defense counsel unless and until the plaintiff has been exonerated by direct appeal, post-conviction relief, or otherwise. The doctrine defers accrual of the malpractice cause of action until exoneration.

Practical effect: Claims 5 and 6 (malpractice and breach of fiduciary duty against Holub and Brad) are preserved now via this ledger and by the pending State Bar of Texas grievances, but cannot be filed as civil suits until Kyle's criminal cases resolve favorably. The State Bar grievances proceed independently — the Peeler doctrine does not bar disciplinary proceedings, and the operator has already filed grievances against both attorneys.

Parallel effect on Claims 7 (malicious prosecution) and 2 (fabrication-of-evidence § 1983): both require favorable termination of the criminal case. All three families of claims should be calendared to launch immediately upon acquittal, dismissal, or reversal.

Rules of Engagement (Operator Discipline)

  • Always file in writing. Oral complaints do not create a record.
  • Always obtain a stamped, receipted, or portal-confirmed copy at the moment of filing.
  • Always calendar the response window (varies by agency: 30 days is a common floor).
  • Always cross-reference every filing to the master Dossier and to the Civil Suit Running Tally.
  • Never rely on a single channel. Parallel filings compress agency response time and preserve alternative fora.
  • Never make oral commitments. If asked to speak by phone, request the question in writing.
  • Escalate only after documented non-response. Premature escalation dilutes the record.
  • Verify every officeholder name at the time of filing. Titles are stable; names change.

05. 12-Motion Gap Audit

ProphetFuel™ AiOS | ZeroPoint PureLogic™

Twelve-Motion Gap Audit

Ineffective Assistance of Counsel · Sixth Amendment · Kyle Scott Harris

All Signal. Zero Noise.

Prepared 2026-09-03 · Complainant: Troy DanDurand, Friend and Legal Researcher, for Kyle Scott Harris

Legal Research Only · Not Legal Advice · Attorney Work Product · Confidential

To Yahweh The Glory

Executive Summary

Kyle Scott Harris is a pretrial detainee held at Travis County Correctional Complex, Del Valle, Texas, facing three felony-and-Class-A cause numbers in Travis County and four active cause numbers in Collin County. Every one of the twelve pretrial motions catalogued in this audit is standard, expected, and non-controversial defense work in a Texas Assault Family Violence — Impede Breath / Circulation, Terroristic Threat, and Unlawful Restraint prosecution. Public examination of the docket in each of the seven cause numbers listed below shows that Kyle's two court-appointed attorneys — Christopher Willia Holub (Travis County) and John B. "Brad" (Collin County) — have prepared, filed, and set for hearing zero of these twelve motions.

Under Strickland v. Washington, 466 U.S. 668 (1984), a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel is violated when (1) counsel's performance falls below an objective standard of reasonableness under prevailing professional norms, and (2) there is a reasonable probability that, but for counsel's unprofessional errors, the result of the proceeding would have been different. A twelve-for-twelve failure to file standard pretrial defense motions in a case with recanting complainant testimony, unproduced discovery, exculpatory Short Message Service [SMS] evidence, and unindicted third-party witness leverage is a textbook Strickland record. Both prongs are met on the face of the docket.

This audit exists to (a) serve as Exhibit A to Texas State Bar grievances filed with the Office of the Chief Disciplinary Counsel against each named public defender, (b) serve as Exhibit A to a Texas Commission on Judicial Conduct complaint against any presiding judge who signed off on this pretrial record without inquiry, (c) serve as an evidentiary appendix to the parallel sworn criminal complaints already prepared for the Collin County Sheriff, Melissa Police Department, and Travis County Sheriff, and (d) serve as a ready-to-fire pretrial motion queue for retained counsel of record, so that no additional days are lost identifying what should be filed the day new counsel appears.

Sixth Amendment — Ineffective Assistance of Counsel Frame

Strickland v. Washington, 466 United States 83 (1984) — two-prong test.

Prong One — Deficient Performance: Counsel's representation fell below an objective standard of reasonableness under prevailing professional norms. Prevailing norms in a Texas Assault Family Violence — Impede Breath / Circulation prosecution require, at minimum, the twelve motions catalogued below. Zero filings is not a strategic choice — no reasonable Texas criminal defense attorney, exercising ordinary professional skill and diligence, would decline to file any of these motions in a case with the evidentiary profile of Kyle's.

Prong Two — Prejudice: Reasonable probability the outcome would differ. The recantation Short Message Service [SMS] from Bobbi Jo to Beth Martin ("I sent an email to the District Attorney stating that this never happened"), if produced under a Michael Morton Act demand and preserved under a chain-of-custody motion, is directly outcome-determinative on the felony impede-breath charge. The prejudice prong is met on the face of the record.

Corresponding Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct violated on the face of the docket:

  • Rule 1.01 — Competent and Diligent Representation. A lawyer shall not accept or continue employment in a legal matter which the lawyer knows or should know is beyond the lawyer's competence.
  • Rule 1.03 — Communication. A lawyer shall keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and promptly comply with reasonable requests for information.
  • Rule 1.04 — Fees / Diligence. A lawyer shall not neglect a legal matter entrusted to the lawyer.

The Twelve Motions — Element-Mapped Gap Audit

Each motion below states: (a) the motion, (b) the controlling statute or case, (c) why it is customarily expected of competent defense counsel given Kyle's specific charges and evidentiary posture (offered as pattern evidence, not as a claim that the motion is mandatory as a matter of law), (d) what its filing would have produced or prevented, and (e) the docket status in the seven cause numbers of record.

01 Michael Morton Act Discovery Demand Not Filed

Authority: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 39.14 (as amended by Michael Morton Act, 2013)

Customarily expected because: Article 39.14 imposes a continuing, statutory duty on the State to produce, on request, any offense report, witness statement, physical or documentary evidence in the State's possession. The demand is a written request — refusing to send it is not a strategy, it is neglect.

What it produces: Bodycam, dashcam, computer-aided-dispatch [CAD] records, prior statements of Bobbi Jo, any 911 audio, all internal notes on complainant recantation, and — critically — the Bobbi Jo → District Attorney recantation email that Bobbi Jo herself confirmed she sent.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: Every downstream motion (suppression, in limine, cross-examination, sever) is starved of the record it needs to be pled with specificity. The State keeps the recantation evidence off the docket by default.

02 Brady / Giglio Exculpatory and Impeachment Disclosure Demand Not Filed

Authority: Brady v. Maryland, 373 United States 83 (1963); Giglio v. United States, 405 United States 150 (1972); Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 39.14(h)

Customarily expected because: The prosecution has a constitutional duty to disclose evidence favorable to the accused that is material either to guilt or punishment. A written Brady/Giglio demand triggers the prosecutor's obligation to search for and produce impeachment material — prior inconsistent statements, benefits promised to witnesses, and law-enforcement misconduct histories.

What it produces: Bobbi Jo's recantation email, any promises made in exchange for her original statement, any prior inconsistent statements, and any impeachment record on the investigating officers.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: The recantation SMS to Beth Martin ("I sent an email to the District Attorney stating that this never happened") is precisely the material Brady was written to protect. Not demanding it in writing means it never enters the record.

03 Motion for Bond Reduction / Personal Recognizance Bond Not Filed

Authority: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 17.15; Tex. Const. Art. I, § 11

Customarily expected because: Article 17.15 requires bail to be sufficient to give reasonable assurance of appearance, no higher than necessary, not oppressive, and set with reference to ability to pay. A defendant sitting in jail through multiple settings without a bond-reduction hearing has been abandoned on the most reversible pretrial issue in Texas criminal procedure.

What it produces: Either release, a lowered bond, or a pretrial-services alternative — any of which enables meaningful defense preparation, private witness contact, and mitigation development.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: Kyle remains in Travis County Correctional Complex, 3614 Bill Price Road, Del Valle, unable to assist in his own defense, unable to contact witnesses, and unable to develop mitigation — while the recantation record ages.

04 Motion to Suppress Statements — Miranda / Article 38.22 Not Filed

Authority: Miranda v. Arizona, 384 United States 436 (1966); Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 38.22

Customarily expected because: Article 38.22 imposes stricter warning and recording requirements than federal Miranda. Any custodial statement not fully compliant is inadmissible. In a case where the State's proof leans on scene statements, testing suppression is baseline defense practice.

What it produces: A pretrial hearing at which the State must produce the arresting officers, lay foundation for admissibility of every statement, and expose contradiction with bodycam and dashcam recordings.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: Any statement Kyle made scene-side stands unchallenged and admissible without ever having been tested against the recording record.

05 Motion in Limine — Texas Rule of Evidence 404(b) Extraneous Offenses Not Filed

Authority: Tex. R. Evid. 404(b); Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 37.07 § 3(g)

Customarily expected because: The State is barred from parading prior bad acts before the jury absent notice and a permissible non-character purpose. A motion in limine forces disclosure of the State's Rule 404(b) list pretrial, allowing the defense to litigate admissibility at a Rule 403 balancing hearing, out of the jury's hearing.

What it produces: An itemized list of any prior-relationship or extraneous-offense material the State intends to use, with a pretrial ruling on each item's admissibility.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: In a family-violence prosecution, the State's routine strategy is to introduce "cycle of violence" or "prior relationship" evidence. Not filing a motion in limine means the defense first learns of these items when the State offers them in front of the jury.

06 Motion for Expert-Witness Funds — Ake v. Oklahoma Not Filed

Authority: Ake v. Oklahoma, 470 United States 68 (1985); Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 26.052 (analog)

Customarily expected because: Indigent defendants have a due-process right to expert assistance when the State's case involves specialized evidence. In an Impede-Breath / Circulation felony, medical testimony on the physical signs of strangulation is the State's strongest tool. The defense is entitled to a countering expert at State expense.

What it produces: Court-appointed medical and forensic experts to review any medical documentation, photographs, and complainant statements — and to opine on absence of injuries consistent with the charged conduct.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: The State's medical narrative goes uncontested. Defense counsel cannot cross-examine specialized witnesses without a specialized foundation of their own.

07 Motion for Grand Jury Transcripts and Testimony Not Filed

Authority: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 20A.201–20A.204 (grand jury records); Tex. R. Evid. 615

Customarily expected because: Grand jury testimony is a first-in-time sworn statement. Inconsistency between grand jury testimony and trial testimony is direct impeachment material. Requesting the transcript pretrial gives the defense a locked-in prior statement to cross-examine on.

What it produces: Bobbi Jo's grand jury testimony (assuming the felony indictment issued through grand jury proceedings) — which, given her post-charge recantation, is likely to contain material inconsistencies impeaching any live testimony the State may attempt to elicit.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: No locked-in prior statement in defense hands. Cross-examination proceeds without the strongest impeachment tool.

08 Motion to Compel Outcry-Witness Disclosure Not Filed

Authority: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 38.072 (outcry witness in family-violence cases)

Customarily expected because: Article 38.072 requires the State, on request, to identify its outcry witness and produce the statement pretrial. A pretrial hearing tests reliability. Not filing means the outcry testimony arrives at trial unchallenged.

What it produces: Identity of the first-outcry witness, a written summary of the outcry statement, and a reliability hearing at which the defense can cross-examine outcry recipient and complainant.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: If the State intends to use hearsay outcry testimony to fill in gaps left by Bobbi Jo's recantation, that strategy proceeds unchallenged.

09 Motion for Defensive-Issues Character Evidence — Rule 404(a)(2) Not Filed

Authority: Tex. R. Evid. 404(a)(2); Tex. R. Evid. 405

Customarily expected because: The defense may offer evidence of a pertinent character trait of the accused, and — critically — evidence of a pertinent trait of the complainant (e.g., prior aggression). Filing puts the State on notice and permits early ruling on the defensive character theory.

What it produces: A pretrial ruling on defensive character evidence and the opportunity to develop mitigation, provocation, and self-defense frames.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: The defensive character theory is never developed on the record. The jury never hears mitigation the Rules of Evidence expressly permit.

10 Speedy Trial Demand — Sixth Amendment and Article 17.151 Not Filed

Authority: United States Constitution, Sixth Amendment and Fourteenth Amendment; Tex. Const. Art. I, § 10; Barker v. Wingo, 407 U.S. 514 (1972) (four-factor balancing analysis); Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 17.151 (release / reduced-bail remedy where State is not ready within 90 days for a felony or 30 days for a qualifying Class A). Note: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 32A.02 is dead law — voided by Meshell v. State, 739 S.W.2d 246 (Tex. Crim. App. 1987) and repealed by Acts 2005, 79th Leg., Ch. 828; it supplies no operative right or clock and is not cited.

Customarily expected because: The Sixth Amendment right to a speedy trial attaches at arrest. Formal written demand marks the record — under Barker v. Wingo, 407 U.S. 514 (1972), assertion of the right is one of four factors in the balancing test. Failure to assert weighs against the defendant in the Barker analysis.

What it produces: A dated, on-the-record demand that starts running the delay-attribution clock in Kyle's favor and pressures the State to try the case or dismiss.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: The State controls the calendar without defense pressure while Kyle sits in custody. Time favors the State.

11 Motion to Sever Joined Offenses Not Filed

Authority: Tex. Penal § 3.04 (severance right in consolidated prosecutions); Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 21.24

Customarily expected because: Where multiple offenses are consolidated for trial, the defendant has a right to severance on demand under § 3.04 in most circumstances. Trying three charges together to the same jury on a family-violence complainant's recanted account maximizes prejudicial spillover.

What it produces: Separate trials on Impede Breath, Terroristic Threat, and Unlawful Restraint — forcing the State to prove each cause on its own evidentiary footing.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: Prejudicial cross-charge inference goes to the jury without defense objection preserved.

12 Motion to Preserve Evidence and Compel Chain-of-Custody — Bobbi Jo Devices and Recantation SMS Not Filed

Authority: Arizona v. Youngblood, 488 United States 51 (1988); Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 38.43 (biological evidence preservation as analog); Tex. Penal § 37.09 (tampering with evidence — criminalizes destruction by anyone with notice)

Customarily expected because: Once the defense has notice of specific exculpatory material (the Bobbi Jo → Beth Martin recantation SMS thread, the Bobbi Jo → District Attorney recantation email), a written preservation motion converts destruction of that evidence from "loss" into evidence-tampering exposure for whoever destroys it.

What it produces: On-the-record notice to the State, complainant, and any third-party custodian that the identified electronic communications must be preserved in native format with full metadata pending court order.

Kyle-specific consequence of non-filing: The single strongest defense exhibit — Bobbi Jo's own written recantation — can disappear or be "device-lost" with no evidence-tampering exposure attaching, because no preservation demand ever put anyone on notice.

Five Whys — Why This Cannot Be Strategic Silence

Root-Cause Analysis

Why 1 — Why were zero motions filed? Because counsel did not draft, calendar, or submit any of the standard pretrial motions expected in a Texas Assault Family Violence — Impede prosecution.

Why 2 — Why did counsel not draft them? There is no strategic rationale in the record explaining the omission. Every one of these twelve motions produces information asymmetrically favorable to the defense at zero litigation risk — filing is nearly costless, refusing to file cedes ground.

Why 3 — Why cede ground at zero cost? The only remaining explanations are: (a) neglect, (b) caseload overwhelm, (c) failure to review the recantation record, or (d) systemic public-defender capacity failure. None of these are constitutional strategy — all are Sixth Amendment deficiency.

Why 4 — Why did no supervising authority correct the omission? The presiding court, docket clerk, and county public-defender oversight structure either did not detect the twelve-for-twelve gap or detected it and did not act. Either failure independently supports a Texas Commission on Judicial Conduct inquiry.

Why 5 — Why does the system permit this pattern? Because absent a Sixth Amendment ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claim, a Texas State Bar grievance, and a public docket audit, no institutional actor is measured against the standard-of-care metric this document establishes. This audit exists to force the measurement.

Relief Roadmap

This audit is the evidentiary foundation for four parallel instruments:

  1. Texas State Bar Grievance — Christopher Willia Holub. Filed with the Office of the Chief Disciplinary Counsel, State Bar of Texas. Attaches this audit as Exhibit A. Alleges violations of Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct 1.01, 1.03, and 1.04.
  2. Texas State Bar Grievance — John B. "Brad". Parallel filing, same attachment, same rule set.
  3. Texas Commission on Judicial Conduct Complaint. Filed conditionally, upon confirmation that the presiding judge in one or more of the seven cause numbers held pretrial settings without inquiry into the standard-of-care motion gap.
  4. Ready-Fire Motion Queue for Successor Counsel. When retained counsel appears, this audit doubles as a work-plan: twelve motions, twelve drafting outlines, twelve statutory anchors — pretrial defense begins on Day One of new representation, not Day Thirty.

SCOPE WARNING — STATE-SIDE ATTRIBUTION VECTOR. The Durable Power of Attorney [DPOA] is the single §12 instrument the State most wants the Principal to execute. Once executed, subsequent Agent acts and communications become materially easier to attribute, authenticate, and subpoena under agency principles and Texas Rule of Evidence 801(e)(2)(C) and 801(e)(2)(D) party-opponent attribution. If the Agent thereafter touches the complaining witness, other witnesses, records custodians, agencies, or discovery-holders, the State's litigation posture under Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 38.49 (forfeiture-by-wrongdoing) is materially strengthened by the pre-existing agency record. Mandatory scope-narrowing before execution: (i) grant powers only for non-litigation administrative matters — mail handling, banking, digital-account access, veterinary and jail-administrative correspondence, records requests, filing of civil chattel-recovery instruments; (ii) expressly exclude authority to communicate substantively with the complaining witness, any prosecutor, any court, any State discovery-holder, or any journalist/blogger; (iii) expressly exclude any litigation-agency or criminal-defense-strategy authority (retained solely by the Principal and counsel-of-record); (iv) explicitly reserve the Principal's right to revoke in writing at any time under Tex. Estates Code § 751.0021.

07. How-To — Attorney Visitation (TCSO)

How-To — Attorney Visitation Registration
Travis County Sheriff's Office · Privileged Phone + Video · Dossier Reference
Facility: Travis County Correctional Complex, Del Valle, Texas  ·  Client of Reference: Kyle Scott Harris  ·  Cause: D-1-DC-25-303689  ·  Live-Fetch Verified: 2026-09-03

1 · Purpose

General reference section describing the two-step registration required for any Texas-licensed attorney to conduct confidential, non-recorded, attorney-client-privileged legal phone calls and legal video visits with any incarcerated client held at the Travis County Correctional Complex. The Travis County Sheriff's Office [TCSO] uses two separate systems — ViaPath Technologies (video / Global Tel Link [GTL]) and the TCSO Private Do-Not-Record Phone List — and each requires its own attorney registration. Filed in the dossier as a standing reference for any attorney of record who is not already registered.

2 · Primary-Source Verification

Verified URLs (live-fetch 2026-09-03):

  • https://www.tcsheriff.org/inmate-jail-info/attorney-info/attorney-contact — TCSO Attorney Contact page.
  • https://www.gtlvisitme.com/app — ViaPath Technologies (formerly Global Tel Link) Travis County Visitation Scheduling portal.
  • https://www.gettingout.com/ — ViaPath GettingOut companion portal for account setup + video-visit management.
  • https://www.traviscountytx.gov/county-attorney/privileged-communications — Travis County Attorney privileged-communications policy reference.

3 · Confidentiality Warning — Verbatim from TCSO

Primary-source notice, verbatim:

"ALL conversations to phone numbers and/or persons that are NOT REGISTERED as attorneys on the TCSO Private Do Not Record List ARE SUBJECT TO RECORDING."

Operational implication: Until both registrations below are complete and TCSO has confirmed the destination number is on the Do-Not-Record list, any inmate-originated call to that number will be recorded and may be reviewed by the Sheriff's Office or subpoenaed by the prosecution. Privileged conversation must not be conducted on an unregistered line.

4 · Step A — Video Visit Registration (ViaPath / GTL Portal)

  1. Go to https://www.gtlvisitme.com/app.
  2. Select Travis County (Texas) from the facility list.
  3. Create an account under attorney status — use bar-registered legal name and law-firm email.
  4. During account setup, expressly select the attorney / legal-professional visit-type. This is the flag that routes the visit to the confidential attorney channel rather than the general public visitation queue.
  5. Upload requested credentials as prompted (typically bar card scan + government photo identification). If the portal does not prompt for credential upload, phone TCSO Visitation Personnel at 512-854-4666 to confirm the credential-submission channel and forward credentials by the method specified.
  6. Once approved, schedule a video visit under the attorney visit-type. Client-side, the visit occurs on a jail-side video terminal; attorney-side, it can be conducted from any Apple iPhone, iPad, iPod Touch, Android smartphone or tablet, or a computer with high-speed internet access.

5 · Step B — Phone "Do-Not-Record" Registration (Separate System)

  1. Phone TCSO Visitation Personnel at 512-854-4666.
  2. Identify as attorney of record for the incarcerated client (client full legal name + cause number).
  3. Request that the direct office phone number and any additional office lines to be used be added to the TCSO Private Do-Not-Record List for attorney communication.
  4. Provide the credentials TCSO requests — typically full legal name, State Bar of Texas card number, law-firm mailing address, direct-dial number(s) to be registered, and government photo identification. Confirm the submission channel (email, fax, in-person, or portal upload) at the time of the call.
  5. Request written confirmation (email is acceptable) when the number(s) have been added to the Do-Not-Record list. Retain the confirmation for the file.

6 · Attorney-Client Privilege Protections Once Registered

  • Inmate-originated attorney calls, once the destination number is on the Do-Not-Record List, are not recorded and are not monitored by TCSO.
  • Standard attorney call duration cap per call: twenty (20) minutes per source; calls to attorneys are free of charge to the inmate.
  • Video visits scheduled through ViaPath under the attorney visit-type are conducted through the confidential attorney channel and are not recorded when properly flagged.
  • Any recording anomaly, monitoring exception, or unauthorized disclosure of an attorney call or video visit should be documented immediately, preserved (screenshot of any confirmation of Do-Not-Record status; call log; scheduling record), and treated as a Sixth Amendment / Fifth Amendment intrusion event that may support a motion to suppress and a Brady disclosure demand.

7 · Verified Contacts (Live-Fetch 2026-09-03)

LineNumberHours
TCSO Visitation Personnel512-854-4666Business hours (Central)

8 · Failure Modes — What Can Break Privilege

  • Unregistered phone number. Call recorded by default. Solution: complete Step B before first privileged call.
  • Public visit-type selected in ViaPath instead of attorney visit-type. Visit routed through public channel with recording. Solution: select attorney visit-type at every booking; verify at scheduling confirmation.
  • Credential lapse. Bar-card renewal not on file with TCSO can silently drop the Do-Not-Record flag. Solution: annual re-verification with TCSO Visitation Personnel.
  • Third-party joining the call. Adding an unregistered non-attorney to a call or video visit can be construed as waiving privilege as to that portion. Solution: keep attorney-client calls and visits attorney-and-client only; conduct any coordination with third parties (paralegals, investigators, agents-in-fact) on separate unprivileged channels or route the third-party attendance under a written joint-defense / common-interest agreement.
  • Facility system anomaly. If TCSO or ViaPath system flags a "recording error" or unexpected recording alert during a privileged call, terminate the call, document the anomaly in writing within 24 hours, and route a preservation-and-disclosure demand to TCSO.

9 · Dossier Registration

This section is filed in the Kyle-Signed Instrument Dossier as a standing How-To reference. It is not a signed instrument, does not require Kyle's signature or notarization, and is available for any attorney of record to consult as needed. Cross-referenced from Master Index § 6 (Attorney-Coordination Reference).
