Purpose of This Package

This package contains four separate legal instruments prepared for execution by Kyle Scott Harris, currently in pretrial custody at the Travis County Correctional Complex in Del Valle, Texas. Each instrument authorizes Troy DanDurand to act on the Principal's behalf within the scope stated in that instrument. The four instruments together give the Agent the practical authority needed to move records requests, communicate with defense counsel, manage financial and property matters that cannot be handled from custody, obtain medical information, and coordinate with jail administration. The instruments are separate on purpose. The Principal may execute all four, execute some, or decline any of them. Each instrument may be revoked independently in writing.

09. Instrument 6 — Directive to Prior Veterinarian (Gunner + Nebula)
ProphetFuel™ AiOS  |  ZeroPoint PureLogic™
Directive to Prior Treating Veterinarian
Gunner & Nebula — Records Preservation · Release Restriction · Contact Routing
Declarant / Owner: Kyle Scott Harris
Attorney-in-Fact: Troy DanDurand
Current Custody of Declarant: Travis County Correctional Complex
Underlying Criminal Cause: D-1-DC-25-303689
Date of Notice: 2026-09-03
Instrument: #6 — Directive to Prior Veterinarian

1 · Purpose of This Directive

This document is a formal owner-issued directive and records-preservation notice to any prior treating veterinarian, veterinary clinic, animal hospital, mobile-vet practice, low-cost clinic, or emergency veterinary hospital that examined, vaccinated, sterilized, medicated, hospitalized, boarded, or otherwise provided care to either dog named Gunner or Nebula at any time prior to the intake events described in the accompanying dossier.

This directive is issued in tandem with, and is expressly incorporated by reference into, the following instruments executed by Kyle Scott Harris of even date (2026-09-03): the Durable Statutory Power of Attorney; the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act [HIPAA] Authorization; the Declaration of Ownership — Gunner; the Declaration of Ownership — Nebula; the Reclamation Demand — Gunner; the Preservation Letter — Nebula; the Preservation Letter — Gunner; and the Sworn Rescission of Purported Surrender — Bobbi Jo Rice.

The Preservation Letters listed above bind the attending veterinarian during the Collin County Animal Services custody window and any post-adoption possessor. This Directive closes the remaining gap by binding every prior treating clinic that holds baseline records, vaccination history, ownership-of-record entries, prior microchip enrollments, and prior identification photographs.

2 · Legal Basis for This Directive

  • Owner authority over veterinary records. Under Texas law, the client of record is the owner of the animal patient. The owner controls release, transfer, and disposition of records absent a lawful court order. See Texas Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners Rules, 22 Tex. Admin. Code § 573.52 (confidentiality of records); Texas Occupations Code Chapter 801 (Veterinary Licensing Act).
  • Agency authority. Restatement (Third) of Agency § 6.01. Attorney-in-Fact acts with full authority of principal under Texas Estates Code Chapter 752 (Statutory Durable Power of Attorney).
  • Property interest in companion animals. Bueckner v. Hamel, 886 S.W.2d 368 (Tex. App. — Houston [1st Dist.] 1994, writ denied).
  • Common-law duty to preserve evidence when litigation is reasonably anticipated. Trevino v. Ortega, 969 S.W.2d 950 (Tex. 1998); Brookshire Bros., Ltd. v. Aldridge, 438 S.W.3d 9 (Tex. 2014); Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. v. Johnson, 106 S.W.3d 718 (Tex. 2003).
  • Void ab initio doctrine. An unauthorized third party cannot ratify her own defective authority. Douglass v. Panama, Inc., 504 S.W.2d 776 (Tex. 1974).
  • Theft by appropriation after demand · Tampering with governmental records · Forgery. Texas Penal Code §§ 31.03, 37.10, 32.21 (predicates if records are altered, released to an unauthorized party, or fabricated to support an unauthorized transfer).

1 · Purpose of This Instruction

This document is a formal written instruction from the client to counsel of record, delivered pursuant to the client's Sixth Amendment right to counsel of choice and the client's authority under the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct to define the objectives and scope of representation. It is directed to Chris Holub, counsel of record for Kyle Scott Harris in Travis County criminal cause D-1-DC-25-303689.

This instruction is issued in tandem with, and is expressly incorporated by reference into, the following instruments executed by Kyle Scott Harris of even date (2026-09-03): the Durable Statutory Power of Attorney (naming Troy DanDurand attorney-in-fact); the Limited Power of Attorney (scope-carve for counsel communications and evidence preservation); the Annex E Visitor Authorization; the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act [HIPAA] Authorization; and every property-recovery and evidence-preservation instrument in the Kyle-Signed Instrument Suite dated 2026-09-03.

2 · Legal Basis for This Instruction

  • Client authority over objectives of representation. Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct [TDRPC] Rule 1.02(a): "a lawyer shall abide by a client's decisions concerning the objectives and general methods of representation."
  • Duty of communication. TDRPC Rule 1.03: "a lawyer shall keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and promptly comply with reasonable requests for information."
  • Duty of confidentiality. TDRPC Rule 1.05.
  • Duty on termination / client-file surrender. Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct [TDRPC] Rule 1.15 (Declining or Terminating Representation), subsection (d): counsel shall, on termination, take reasonable steps to the extent reasonably practicable to protect the client's interests, including surrendering papers and property to which the client is entitled and refunding any advance payment of fee that has not been earned. (Prior draft mislabeled this rule as 1.15 duty-of-safekeeping; the operative withdrawal-duty rule in Texas is TDRPC 1.15 titled "Declining or Terminating Representation." Federal ABA Model Rule numbering places these duties at Rule 1.16; Texas retains them at Rule 1.15 with the same substantive content. Counsel to verify current rule text at time of withdrawal.)
  • Sixth Amendment right to counsel of choice. United States v. Gonzalez-Lopez, 548 U.S. 140 (2006).
  • Texas Fair Defense Act. Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 1.051 (right to counsel and appointment of counsel).
  • Discovery in criminal cases (Michael Morton Act). Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 39.14 (disclosure, retention, and preservation of evidence).
  • Agency authority. Restatement (Third) of Agency § 6.01. Attorney-in-Fact acts with full authority of principal under Texas Estates Code Chapter 752 (Statutory Durable Power of Attorney).

3 · Directive One — Affirmative Actions Counsel Is Instructed to Take

  1. Recognize the Attorney-in-Fact of record. Chris Holub is instructed to recognize Troy DanDurand as the client's Attorney-in-Fact under the Durable Statutory Power of Attorney executed of even date, for all non-privileged administrative, logistical, discovery-preservation, records-request, correspondence, bond, jail-administration, and evidence-preservation matters.
  2. Communicate with the Attorney-in-Fact. Counsel is instructed to accept, return, and initiate communications with the Attorney-in-Fact on non-privileged administrative matters, and to route status updates, discovery notifications, motion filings, hearing settings, and calendar changes to the Attorney-in-Fact by electronic mail with delivery receipt requested and by telephone at the number on file.
  3. Preserve the client file. Counsel is instructed to preserve, without alteration, redaction, purge, transfer to any successor practice, or routine-cycle destruction, the complete client file in the underlying cause, including intake notes, correspondence, discovery, investigator work-product, notes of witness interviews, notes of client meetings, notes of prosecutor calls, notes of court appearances, billing records, and every draft motion or memorandum, until final adjudication of every civil, administrative, and criminal proceeding arising from the underlying cause.
  4. Preserve and demand discovery under Art. 39.14. Counsel is instructed to preserve every disclosure received and to demand from the State every discoverable item under Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 39.14, including but not limited to arrest reports, offense reports, body-worn-camera recordings, dash-camera recordings, jail intake and booking recordings, jail medical records, laboratory reports, chain-of-custody records, witness statements, and every item of exculpatory, mitigating, or impeaching evidence under Brady v. Maryland, 373 U.S. 83 (1963).
  5. Substantive-motion posture.   7. Speedy-trial posture. Counsel is instructed to preserve the client's speedy-trial rights under the Sixth Amendment and Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, Tex. Const. Art. I § 10, the Barker v. Wingo, 407 U.S. 514 (1972) four-factor analysis, and the separate release / reduced-bail remedy of Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 17.151, and to secure the client's advance written concurrence before agreeing to any continuance or reset that would toll the speedy-trial clock. Counsel shall NOT cite Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 32A.02 — that statute is dead law per Meshell v. State, 739 S.W.2d 246 (Tex. Crim. App. 1987) and was repealed by Acts 2005, 79th Leg., Ch. 828.
  8. Indigency reaffirmation posture. Counsel is instructed to preserve and, on client request, refile the client's indigency affidavit under Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 26.04 to secure continued appointment or to defeat any State motion to disqualify appointed counsel.
  9. Character-evidence coordination. Counsel is instructed to coordinate with the Attorney-in-Fact on the assembly and preservation of client-favorable character evidence, including employment history, military service history (if any), family testimony, community-service records, and religious-affiliation records.
  10. Servicemembers Civil Relief Act [SCRA] coordination. If military-status intake conducted by the Attorney-in-Fact confirms client eligibility under 50 U.S.C. §§ 3901–4043, counsel is instructed to coordinate the client's SCRA posture in every civil proceeding collateral to this cause.   8. Do not destroy, purge, archive-out, migrate-off, or transfer to any successor practice any physical or electronic client-file record without preserving a complete copy accessible to the client and the Attorney-in-Fact on request.
  9. Do not back-date, forward-date, re-draft, re-format, or annotate any existing client-file entry other than by dated, signed addendum that leaves the original entry visible and legible.
  10. Do not disclose the existence, contents, or receipt of this instruction to any third party absent the client's or the Attorney-in-Fact's advance written consent.

1 · Purpose of This Affidavit

This is a sworn reaffirmation of indigency made pursuant to Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 26.04 and the Sixth Amendment right to counsel. 2 · Legal Basis for the Right and the Reaffirmation

  • Sixth Amendment right to counsel. Gideon v. Wainwright, 372 U.S. 335 (1963); Argersinger v. Hamlin, 407 U.S. 25 (1972); Rothgery v. Gillespie County, 554 U.S. 191 (2008) (right to counsel attaches at first initial appearance).
  • Texas Constitution. Tex. Const. Art. I § 10 (right to counsel in all criminal prosecutions).
  • Texas Fair Defense Act. Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 1.051 (right to counsel and appointment of counsel).
  • Indigency determination and appointment procedures. Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 26.04 (indigency determination, appointment of counsel, and continued representation).
  • Compensation of appointed counsel. Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 26.05.
  • Investigator, expert, and interpreter appointment. Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 26.05(a); Ake v. Oklahoma, 470 U.S. 68 (1985) (indigent defendant's right to expert assistance).
  • Right to interpreter. Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 38.30 (interpreters).
  • Custodial indigency presumption. Continued pretrial incarceration is prima facie evidence of continued indigency for purposes of appointed-counsel status.

13. Instrument 10 — Limited Assignment of Claims
ProphetFuel™ AiOS  |  ZeroPoint PureLogic™
Limited Assignment of Claims — Chattel-Recovery Suite
Instrument 10 · Tier 2 · Kyle-Signed Instrument Suite
Assignor: Kyle Scott Harris  ·  Assignee: Troy DanDurand, Attorney-in-Fact  ·  Custody: Travis County Correctional Complex  ·  Underlying Cause: D-1-DC-25-303689  ·  Date: 2026-09-03

1 · Purpose

Kyle Scott Harris ("Assignor"), a pretrial detainee in the custody of the Travis County Sheriff's Office, hereby assigns to Troy DanDurand ("Assignee") a limited, revocable, non-general beneficial interest in specifically enumerated civil claims arising exclusively from the wrongful taking, wrongful destruction, and wrongful conversion of Assignor's companion animals Gunner and Nebula and related evidentiary spoliation, records tampering, and forgery predicates. This assignment is limited to the categories enumerated in Section 4. It confers no general litigation authority, no criminal-defense authority, no waiver of the attorney-client privilege on any matter, and no interest in any claim not specifically listed.

2 · Legal Basis

  • Texas common-law assignability of choses in action for injury to property (Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 317; Southern County Mut. Ins. Co. v. Ochoa, 19 S.W.3d 452 (Tex. App. — Corpus Christi 2000)).
  • Texas Business & Commerce Code § 4.207 (assignability of payment claims).
  • Texas Estates Code Ch. 752 (Statutory Durable Power of Attorney), incorporated by reference from Instrument 1 (DPOA).
  • Restatement (Third) Agency § 6.01 (principal-agent authority scope).
  • Bueckner v. Hamel, 886 S.W.2d 368 (Tex. App. — Houston [1st Dist.] 1994, writ denied) (dogs as chattel with sentimental value).
  • Texas Penal Code § 42.09 (cruelty to non-livestock animals — civil-restitution predicate).
  • 42 U.S.C. § 1983 (procedural due process in seizure and destruction of chattel by state actors).

3 · Ratification of Attorney-in-Fact Status

Assignor ratifies, re-affirms, and re-executes the appointment of Assignee as Attorney-in-Fact under the Texas Statutory Durable Power of Attorney executed contemporaneously herewith (Instrument 1) and the Limited Power of Attorney (Instrument 4). Nothing in this Assignment supersedes, narrows, or expands the powers granted under those instruments. Where authority under the DPOA and under this Assignment overlap, the Assignee may act under either. Where they conflict, the DPOA controls.

4 · Scope of Assignment — Enumerated Claims Only

The assignment is limited to a beneficial interest in the following, and only the following, civil claims and recovery streams:

  1. Conversion of chattel (Gunner) — refusal to return upon lawful reclamation demand per Instrument 12 (Reclamation Demand).
  2. Wrongful destruction of chattel (Nebula) — euthanasia without owner consent, adequate notice, or lawful due-process opportunity to reclaim.
  3. Evidence spoliation (Gunner + Nebula) — destruction, loss, or unavailability of records, samples, remains, communications, or chain-of-custody documentation preserved under Instruments 13 and 14 (Preservation Letters).
  4. Records tampering — false, back-dated, altered, or fabricated entries in any custodial, veterinary, adoption, or surrender record concerning Gunner or Nebula (Tex. Penal Code § 37.10 civil predicate).
  5. Forgery — unauthorized signature on any surrender form, adoption transfer, veterinary consent, or ownership-transfer document purporting to bear the name of Kyle Scott Harris, Bobbi Jo Rice, or any other person as owner (Tex. Penal Code § 32.21 civil predicate).
  6. Theft of chattel — unlawful appropriation of Gunner or Nebula (Tex. Penal Code § 31.03 civil predicate; Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code Ch. 134 Theft Liability Act).
  7. Procedural due-process violation (42 U.S.C. § 1983) — deprivation of a protected property interest in Gunner or Nebula without adequate pre- or post-deprivation process.
  8. Attorney fees, court costs, statutory damages, exemplary damages, and prejudgment interest recoverable in any of the above.

All claims not listed in this Section 4 are expressly retained by Assignor. This Assignment does NOT reach: any criminal-defense matter; any wage claim; any personal-injury claim to Assignor's own person; any inheritance, gift, or trust interest; any real property; any digital asset; any intellectual property; any claim in tort or contract not arising from the Gunner-Nebula chattel-recovery suite.

5 · Assignee Authority — What Assignee May Do

  1. Accept service of process on the enumerated claims on Assignor's behalf, and forward any served papers to counsel of record within seventy-two (72) hours.
  2. Sign settlement releases, dismissals, or covenants-not-to-sue for the enumerated claims only, subject to the concurrence requirement in Section 6.
  3. Endorse settlement checks, insurance-proceeds checks, or restitution checks payable to Assignor for the enumerated claims, and deposit the proceeds into a segregated Assignor-benefit account described in Section 7.
  4. Retain, direct, discharge, and coordinate civil counsel for the enumerated claims.
  5. Execute, deliver, and record any affidavit, notice, demand, or filing supporting the enumerated claims.
  6. Obtain, inspect, copy, and archive any record, document, sample, image, or other tangible thing relevant to the enumerated claims, using the Preservation Letters (Instruments 13, 14), the Reclamation Demand (Instrument 12), and the Rescission of Purported Surrender (Instrument 15) as instruments of recovery.
  7. Coordinate with Chris Holub (Instrument 7) and with Collin County counsel Brad (Instrument 8) on any factual overlap between the enumerated civil claims and any concurrent criminal or civil matter, provided no communication compromises Assignor's attorney-client privilege on any criminal matter.

6 · Concurrence Requirement

Any settlement release, dismissal, or covenant-not-to-sue that would extinguish, waive, or materially compromise any enumerated claim requires Assignor's written concurrence, obtained through one of the three methods below:

  1. In-person visit at Travis County Correctional Complex (or successor facility of incarceration) with the concurrence memorialized in writing and signed by Assignor during the visit; OR
  2. Privileged legal video visit or privileged legal phone call between Assignor and Assignee's designated writing witness (a licensed Texas attorney or notary), with the concurrence transcribed contemporaneously and mailed to Assignor for signature by return mail; OR
  3. Written communication mailed to Assignor at the facility, returned executed by Assignor via facility mail, within thirty (30) calendar days.

Emergency exception: if a court-imposed deadline requires action within a window shorter than the concurrence turnaround above, Assignee may act to preserve the claim (file, oppose, or defer) but shall NOT sign a release, dismissal, or covenant-not-to-sue without Assignor's written concurrence obtained by one of the three methods above.

7 · Segregated Proceeds Account

Any proceeds recovered under the enumerated claims shall be deposited into a segregated non-commingled account bearing the caption "Kyle Scott Harris Chattel-Recovery Suite — Trust for Benefit of Assignor," held by Assignee as a fiduciary. Assignee shall maintain a written ledger of every deposit, disbursement, and outstanding balance and shall provide a written accounting to Assignor within thirty (30) days of any deposit or disbursement, and in any event no less than quarterly. Assignee shall not disburse funds from the segregated account for Assignee's own benefit, for Assignee's compensation, or for any purpose other than: (a) payment of court-approved counsel fees, expert fees, or court costs on the enumerated claims; (b) restitution or repair of any recovered chattel; (c) Assignor's benefit as directed by Assignor in writing. No such account shall be commingled with Assignee's business or personal funds.

8 · No Compensation to Assignee

Assignee acts under this Assignment without compensation. Assignee's role is administrative, coordinative, and preservative. Assignee is not funding Assignor's criminal defense and receives no fee, retainer, contingency, or reimbursement for services performed as Attorney-in-Fact or as Assignee, except reimbursement at cost for out-of-pocket certified-mail, notary, filing-fee, or copying expenses incurred in furtherance of the enumerated claims, documented and reported in the quarterly accounting under Section 7. This provision is incorporated into and reinforces the Sworn Reaffirmation of Indigency (Instrument 9) and shall not be construed to affect Assignor's indigency status for purposes of Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 26.04 or Art. 26.05.

9 · Revocability

Assignor may revoke this Assignment, in whole or in part, at any time, by written notice signed by Assignor and delivered to Assignee by any reasonable means, including facility mail, in-person delivery during a visit, or notarized statement transmitted through counsel. Revocation is effective on receipt by Assignee. Revocation does not unwind any action already taken in good faith by Assignee prior to receipt, but the proceeds of any completed recovery shall be transferred to Assignor or Assignor's designee within thirty (30) days of receipt of revocation.

10 · Duration

This Assignment endures until: (a) written revocation by Assignor per Section 9; (b) final judgment, settlement, or dismissal of every enumerated claim, followed by disbursement of any proceeds and delivery of a final written accounting; (c) death or incapacity of Assignor, in which case authority terminates and the segregated account shall pass to Assignor's estate; or (d) death, incapacity, or resignation of Assignee, in which case the successor Attorney-in-Fact named in Instrument 1 (Statutory DPOA) shall succeed to the powers herein.

11 · Incorporation by Reference

The following Kyle-Signed instruments are incorporated herein by reference and shall be read as one integrated authority: Statutory Durable Power of Attorney (Instrument 1); Limited Power of Attorney (Instrument 4); Directive to Prior Treating Veterinarian (Instrument 6); Written Instruction to Counsel — Holub (Instrument 7); Written Instruction to Counsel — Brad (Instrument 8); Sworn Reaffirmation of Indigency (Instrument 9); Declaration of Ownership — Gunner (Instrument 10 in field-carry roster, renumbered from prior 9); Declaration of Ownership — Nebula (Instrument 11); Reclamation Demand — Gunner (Instrument 12); Preservation Letters — Nebula (Instrument 13); Preservation Letter — Gunner (Instrument 14); Sworn Rescission of Purported Surrender — Bobbi Jo Rice (Instrument 15).

12 · Reservation of Rights

Assignor reserves every right, remedy, defense, and cause of action not expressly assigned herein. Nothing in this Assignment shall be construed as a waiver of Assignor's Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination, Sixth Amendment right to counsel, right to remain silent, right to a jury trial, right to due process, right to be free from unreasonable search and seizure, right to petition, right to counsel of choice, or any right protected by the Constitution of the United States, the Constitution of the State of Texas, or any statute of the United States or the State of Texas. Assignor's cooperation with the enumerated civil claims does not concede any fact, admission, or waiver in any criminal matter.

14. Instrument 11 — Digital Account Written Direction
ProphetFuel™ AiOS  |  ZeroPoint PureLogic™
Digital-Account Written Direction
Instrument 11 · Tier 3 · Kyle-Signed Instrument Suite
Principal: Kyle Scott Harris  ·  Designated Fiduciary: Troy DanDurand, Attorney-in-Fact  ·  Custody: Travis County Correctional Complex  ·  Underlying Cause: D-1-DC-25-303689  ·  Date: 2026-09-03

1 · Purpose

Kyle Scott Harris ("Principal"), a pretrial detainee in the custody of the Travis County Sheriff's Office, directs the disclosure to and preservation, freeze, and administrative management by Troy DanDurand ("Designated Fiduciary") of every digital account, digital asset, and electronic communication of the Principal enumerated or implicated herein, for the limited purposes of preservation of evidence, prevention of dissipation, prevention of identity theft, continuity of essential bill payment where funds exist, and orderly administration during the period of pretrial custody. This Direction is a written record of the Principal's express consent under the Texas Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act [TRUFADAA], the Stored Communications Act [SCA], the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act [CFAA] scope-of-authorization framework, and applicable custodian terms-of-service, and is intended to compel custodian disclosure of both the catalog of the Principal's electronic communications and (where expressly checked below) the content thereof.

2 · Legal Basis

  • Texas Estates Code Chapter 2001 — Texas Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act [TRUFADAA], §§ 2001.001 et seq. (governs designated-fiduciary access to catalog and content of electronic communications and digital assets).
  • Texas Estates Code §§ 2001.102-2001.104 (online-tool + record priority; principal's written direction controls where the custodian has no online tool or where principal expressly overrides the online tool).
  • Stored Communications Act, 18 U.S.C. §§ 2701-2712 (custodian may disclose content of electronic communications with lawful consent of the originator or an addressee, and to any person as directed by an authorized fiduciary under state law).
  • Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, 18 U.S.C. § 1030 (scope of authorization; principal's written grant of authority to fiduciary precludes CFAA "exceeds authorized access" theory as to enumerated actions).
  • Texas Estates Code Chapter 752 (Statutory Durable Power of Attorney), incorporated by reference from Instrument 1.
  • Restatement (Third) Agency § 6.01 (principal-agent authority scope).
  • Texas Business & Commerce Code § 521 (identity-theft protection framework).
  • Bank Secrecy Act, 31 U.S.C. § 5311 et seq. and 31 C.F.R. Chapter X (financial-institution reporting obligations informing preservation and hold requests).

3 · Designated Fiduciary Status

Troy DanDurand is the Principal's Attorney-in-Fact under the Texas Statutory Durable Power of Attorney (Instrument 1) and Limited Power of Attorney (Instrument 4) and is expressly designated the Principal's "designated fiduciary" as defined in Tex. Est. Code § 2001.002 for purposes of every custodian named or implicated in this Direction. Where any custodian offers or maintains an online-tool designation form (e.g., Google Inactive Account Manager, Facebook Legacy Contact, Apple Digital Legacy Contact) and the online-tool designation conflicts with this Direction, the Principal expressly OVERRIDES the online tool per Tex. Est. Code § 2001.102(a)(2) and directs that this Direction control. Where the custodian has no online tool or the Principal has not completed one, this Direction is the Principal's written record controlling disclosure and access per Tex. Est. Code § 2001.102(b).

4 · Enumerated Account Categories

The following categories are subject to this Direction, whether or not the Principal has itemized a specific account below. Any account owned, controlled, funded, subscribed, or accessed by the Principal within any listed category is included.

CategoryExamples (non-exhaustive)
A · Financial — depositChecking, savings, money-market, certificate of deposit, credit-union accounts at any bank or credit union.
B · Financial — brokerage / retirementBrokerage, individual retirement account, 401(k), pension, annuity, mutual fund, life insurance with cash value.
C · Financial — peer-to-peer / neobankPayPal, Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, Wise, Revolut, Chime, SoFi, Varo, Current.

5 · Authorized Actions — What Designated Fiduciary May Do

  1. Request from any custodian the catalog of electronic communications and the record of every digital asset held for the Principal per Tex. Est. Code §§ 2001.101, 2001.151.
  2. Request from any custodian the content of electronic communications where the Principal has expressly consented (Section 6 below, checkbox).
  3. View balances, statements, transaction history, and account metadata; download and archive to preserve evidence.
  4. Freeze, place administrative hold on, or request "hold-and-preserve" status on any account to prevent unauthorized access, dissipation, or dispute-window expiry.
  5. Redirect statements, notifications, security alerts, and paper mail to the Designated Fiduciary at DanDurand Enterprises, Inc., 1915 Highway 36 West, PMB 140, Roseville, Minnesota 55113.
  6. Reset passwords, enable two-factor authentication under the Designated Fiduciary's recovery method, and log every credential change with reason and timestamp.
  7. Notify custodians in writing of the Principal's pretrial custody status and continued account ownership; provide certified copies of Instruments 1 (DPOA) and 9 (Reaffirmation of Indigency) as supporting documentation.
  8. Continue payment of essential bills (utilities, storage, mobile carrier, insurance premiums, mortgage / rent, court-approved obligations) from Principal's own funds only, where funds exist, subject to the segregated-accounting duty imported from Instrument 10 (Assignment of Claims) § 7.
  9. Cancel or pause discretionary subscriptions (streaming, gym, non-essential SaaS) to stop dissipation of Principal's funds during custody.
  10. File identity-theft reports with the Federal Trade Commission (IdentityTheft.gov), the three consumer credit reporting agencies (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion), and any implicated custodian in the event of suspected unauthorized access, and place fraud alerts or security freezes on the Principal's consumer credit files.
  11. Retain, direct, and coordinate legal counsel or forensic-technology counsel where custodian refuses lawful disclosure or where litigation is required to compel compliance with TRUFADAA.
  12. Preserve, archive, and copy any content, image, message, video, transaction, or record that may be relevant to the concurrent chattel-recovery suite (Instruments 12-16) or to the criminal defense (via delivery to counsel of record per Instruments 7, 8).

6 · Express Consent to Disclosure of Content — TRUFADAA Trigger

The Principal expressly consents, pursuant to 18 U.S.C. § 2702(b)(3) (Stored Communications Act lawful-consent exception) and Tex. Est. Code § 2001.101, to the disclosure by any custodian of the CONTENT of the Principal's electronic communications, in addition to the catalog thereof, to the Designated Fiduciary, subject to the following category-level scope:

  1. ☒ FULL CONTENT for Categories E (Email), F (Cloud storage), G (Password manager), and M (Government / court) — necessary for evidence preservation, tax compliance, and legal-defense support.
  2. ☒ CATALOG + CONTENT AS RELEVANT for Categories A-D (Financial) — statements, transaction detail, and any communication concerning holds, freezes, disputes, or transfers.
  3. ☒ CATALOG ONLY for Category H (Social / messaging) unless a specific message or thread is subpoenaed, ordered by court, or expressly required for evidence preservation in Instruments 12-16, in which case full content of that specific thread is authorized on a per-instance basis.
  4. ☒ CATALOG + CONTENT AS RELEVANT for Categories I-P as reasonably necessary to execute the authorized actions in Section 5.

Principal initials confirming Section 6 express consent: _______   (Kyle initials)

7 · Prohibited Actions — What Designated Fiduciary Shall NOT Do

  1. Shall NOT sell, transfer, gift, or dissipate any digital asset for the Designated Fiduciary's own benefit.
  2. Shall NOT trade, swap, stake, lend, or speculate with any digital-asset / crypto holding of the Principal. Preservation only. Custodial-exchange holdings shall be moved to withdrawal-only or freeze status pending Principal's release or written direction.
  3. Shall NOT close any account without the Principal's written concurrence obtained by any of the three methods in Instrument 10 § 6 (in-person visit / privileged legal call or video with a writing witness / mailed written concurrence within thirty (30) days), except where the custodian itself initiates closure for its own account-terms reason, in which case the Designated Fiduciary shall preserve all downloadable content first.
  4. Shall NOT open any new account, credit line, loan, credit card, or debt obligation in the Principal's name.
  5. Shall NOT sell, transfer, or gift any non-fungible token, in-game asset, domain, intellectual-property right, or creative work of the Principal.
  6. Shall NOT use, share, or disclose the Principal's credentials, seed phrases, private keys, or authentication tokens to any third party except the Principal, the Principal's counsel of record, or as compelled by lawful court order after opportunity for the Principal to be heard.
  7. Shall NOT commingle the Principal's funds with the Designated Fiduciary's business or personal funds. Payments made on the Principal's behalf shall move directly from the Principal's own account to the payee.
  8. Shall NOT accept compensation for services performed under this Direction, except reimbursement at cost for out-of-pocket expenses documented and reported in the accounting under Section 8.

8 · Accounting Duty

The Designated Fiduciary shall maintain a written ledger of every access event, credential change, freeze / hold placed, notification redirected, payment made, subscription cancelled, and communication with any custodian, and shall provide a written accounting to the Principal quarterly and on demand. The accounting shall itemize by category the balance-at-open, balance-at-close, transactions, and any anomaly detected. This accounting is incorporated into and reinforces the segregated-accounting duty of Instrument 10 § 7 and the no-compensation clause of Instrument 10 § 8.

9 · Custodian Recipients — Written Notice

The Designated Fiduciary shall serve a certified-mail copy of this Direction (with a certified copy of the Statutory Durable Power of Attorney per Instrument 1 attached) on each custodian where the Principal maintains an account within a category above, and shall retain proof of delivery for the file. Where a custodian requires its own institution-specific fiduciary form in addition, the Designated Fiduciary shall complete the institution form under authority of this Direction and attach the Direction and DPOA as supporting exhibits.

10 · Duration and Revocation

This Direction endures from execution until (a) written revocation by the Principal delivered to the Designated Fiduciary by any reasonable means (facility mail, in-person visit, notarized statement through counsel); (b) release of the Principal from pretrial custody and reasonable transition period of thirty (30) days for the Principal to resume account control; (c) death or incapacity of the Principal; or (d) death, incapacity, or resignation of the Designated Fiduciary, in which case the successor Attorney-in-Fact named in Instrument 1 shall succeed to the authorities herein. Revocation is effective on receipt by the Designated Fiduciary. Revocation does not unwind action taken in good faith prior to receipt.

11 · Incorporation by Reference

The following Kyle-Signed instruments are incorporated herein by reference: Statutory Durable Power of Attorney (Instrument 1); HIPAA Authorization (Instrument 3, where a medical-portal account is implicated); Limited Power of Attorney (Instrument 4); Written Instructions to Counsel (Instruments 7 and 8); Sworn Reaffirmation of Indigency (Instrument 9); Limited Assignment of Claims (Instrument 10).

12 · Reservation of Rights

The Principal reserves every right, remedy, defense, and cause of action not expressly granted herein. Nothing in this Direction shall be construed as a waiver of the attorney-client privilege as to any communication with counsel of record, the Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination, the Sixth Amendment right to counsel, or any right protected by the Constitution of the United States, the Constitution of the State of Texas, or any statute of the United States or the State of Texas. Preservation of an electronic communication does not waive any privilege attached to it. Any privileged communication accidentally preserved by the Designated Fiduciary shall be quarantined and returned to counsel of record without further review.

15. Instrument 12 — Mail-Handling Written Direction
ProphetFuel™ AiOS  |  ZeroPoint PureLogic™
Mail-Handling Written Direction
Instrument 12 · Tier 3 · Kyle-Signed Instrument Suite
Principal: Kyle Scott Harris  ·  Designated Mail Agent: Troy DanDurand, Attorney-in-Fact  ·  Custody: Travis County Correctional Complex  ·  Underlying Cause: D-1-DC-25-303689  ·  Date: 2026-09-03

1 · Purpose

Kyle Scott Harris ("Principal"), a pretrial detainee in the custody of the Travis County Sheriff's Office, directs the receipt, opening, scanning, holding, forwarding, orderly administration, and where appropriate response to every item of physical mail, parcel, and courier delivery addressed to the Principal at any Principal-controlled address, by Troy DanDurand ("Designated Mail Agent"), for the limited purposes of preservation of evidence, prevention of default on legal notices, prevention of missed court dates and administrative deadlines, prevention of identity theft, continuity of essential bill payment where funds exist, and orderly administration during the period of pretrial custody. This Direction is a written record of the Principal's express authorization to act as the Principal's agent for mail receipt and handling under United States Postal Service regulation, Texas agency law, and applicable federal mail-tampering carve-outs.

2 · Legal Basis

  • United States Postal Service Regulation 39 C.F.R. § 265.6 — disclosure of postal records to authorized agents of the addressee.
  • United States Postal Service Form 1583 — "Application for Delivery of Mail Through Agent," notarized authorization for a Commercial Mail Receiving Agency or private receiving agent to receive mail on behalf of the addressee.
  • 18 U.S.C. § 1702 — obstruction of correspondence carve-out where receipt is by written authority of the addressee.
  • 18 U.S.C. § 1708 — theft or receipt of stolen mail carve-out where the recipient acts under express written authority.
  • Texas Estates Code Chapter 752 — Statutory Durable Power of Attorney "personal and family maintenance" and "operation of business" powers (incorporated by reference from Instrument 1).
  • Restatement (Third) Agency § 6.01 — scope of actual authority to act on principal's behalf.
  • Texas Government Code Chapter 501 — Texas Department of Criminal Justice and county jail inmate-mail rules (including privileged legal-mail carve-out for attorney correspondence).
  • Travis County Sheriff's Office inmate-mail rules — inbound/outbound mail handling; privileged legal-mail carve-out.
  • Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 521 — identity-theft protection interlock.

3 · Designated Mail Agent Status

The Principal designates Troy DanDurand as his Mail Agent under this Direction and under U.S. Postal Service Form 1583. The Designated Mail Agent is authorized to sign U.S. Postal Service Form 1583 on the Principal's acknowledgment, to present this Direction as evidence of authority at any post office, private mailbox provider, package courier depot, private mail-receiving agency, or registered agent address, and to receive mail addressed to the Principal at every Principal-controlled address enumerated in Section 4.

4 · Enumerated Mail-Address Categories

This Direction covers every item of mail, parcel, envelope, package, courier delivery, notice, and physical correspondence addressed to the Principal at any of the following categories of address. Kyle's specific addresses within each category are collected in the intake at Section 16.

CatAddress CategoryExamples
AResidential address of recordPrincipal's home address on file with U.S. Postal Service and with any government, court, financial, or utility custodian at the date of custody admission.
BPost Office BoxAny U.S. Postal Service P.O. Box rented in Principal's name or Principal-controlled.
CPrivate Mailbox / Commercial Mail Receiving AgencyThe UPS Store mailbox, iPostal1, Anytime Mailbox, Earth Class Mail, or any comparable private mailbox provider.
DRegistered agent addressAny registered-agent address on file for any Principal-owned entity or single-member LLC.
EPrior residential addresses (forwarding window)Any prior address at which mail may still be forwarded under active U.S. Postal Service Change of Address orders (12-month first-class forwarding window per D.M.M. § 507).

5 · Authorized Actions

The Principal authorizes the Designated Mail Agent to perform any and all of the following actions with respect to mail received under this Direction:

  1. Receive. Take physical possession of every item of mail, parcel, envelope, package, and courier delivery addressed to the Principal at any address enumerated in Section 4.
  2. Sign. Sign for certified mail, registered mail, restricted-delivery mail, courier-signature-required deliveries, and any other mail requiring signature, as the Principal's authorized agent.
  3. Open. Open every envelope, parcel, and package, except items marked as privileged legal mail governed by Section 6.
  4. Scan. Scan the outside of each envelope (from + postmark + received date) and every enclosed page to the Dossier at 300 DPI, log sender + received date + scan destination.
  5. Hold. Hold every scanned physical original in a segregated, dated, sender-indexed file at the Agent's business address of record, per Section 8.
  6. Forward to Kyle. Forward copies to the Principal at the Travis County Correctional Complex under Travis County Sheriff's Office inmate-mail rules, subject to facility restrictions on page count, staples, tape, and content.
  7. Forward to counsel. Forward copies of any court, prosecutor, defense-counsel, or agency mail to counsel of record (Chris Holub Travis, Brad Collin) within twenty-four (24) hours of receipt, with a Dossier copy filed same-day.
  8. Discard junk. After scanning and logging, discard true junk mail (unsolicited advertising, pre-approved-credit solicitations, catalog blasts) via cross-cut shredder; retain scan-log entry.
  9. Respond — administrative. Respond to non-legal administrative mail (bill statements, address-confirmation notices, benefits re-enrollment, insurance renewals, utility notices, vehicle-registration notices, tax notices below dispute threshold) under the "personal and family maintenance" and "operation of business" powers of Instrument 1 and Instrument 4.
  10. Route legal mail. Route every piece of mail bearing court seal, prosecutor letterhead, attorney letterhead, agency letterhead, or "Legal Mail" / "Privileged" / "Attorney-Client Communication" marking per the privilege quarantine at Section 6.
  11. Change of Address. File U.S. Postal Service Change of Address orders in the Principal's name to redirect mail from prior residential addresses to a Principal-controlled address of Agent's choosing, and reverse or cancel same on Principal's release or written instruction.

  13. USPS Form 1583. Execute U.S. Postal Service Form 1583 as the Principal's Designated Mail Agent with any post office or private-mailbox provider that requires it, presenting this Direction as evidence of authority.
  14. Identity-theft reports. On detection of any suspicious address change, credential request, or account-open notice, file identity-theft reports with the Federal Trade Commission, Equifax, Experian, TransUnion, and any impacted custodian (interlocks with Instrument 11 § 5).

6 · Legal-Mail Privilege Quarantine

Attorney-marked mail is NOT opened by the Agent. Any envelope bearing:

  • The return address of counsel of record (Chris Holub Travis, Brad Collin, or any successor counsel);
  • The return address of any licensed attorney or law firm;
  • The words "LEGAL MAIL," "PRIVILEGED," "ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION," "WORK PRODUCT," or comparable privilege marking on the outside of the envelope;
  • The return address of any court, court clerk, prosecutor, district attorney, county attorney, United States Attorney, state attorney general, or judicial officer — where the envelope carries an "unopened by non-addressee" or comparable instruction on the face;

— is forwarded unopened to counsel of record (or Principal at facility, if privilege is Principal-directed) within twenty-four (24) hours of receipt, with a face-only scan of the envelope logged to the Dossier and a certified-mail or trackable-courier tracking number recorded. If accidental opening occurs (envelope not marked or marking not observed), the Agent immediately halts reading, seals the item in a new envelope, marks it "OPENED IN ERROR — PRIVILEGE QUARANTINE," logs the incident to the Dossier privilege-quarantine ledger, and forwards to counsel same day.

7 · Prohibited Actions

  1. No opening of privileged mail. Per Section 6.
  2. No forwarding to non-authorized third parties. Mail is forwarded only to Principal, counsel of record, or Dossier storage.
  3. No response to legal mail on Principal's behalf without counsel concurrence. Legal mail is routed to counsel; the Agent may acknowledge receipt to the sender only if counsel directs.
  4. No discard of any item that appears to be legal, court, agency, financial-institution, or evidentiary. When in doubt, hold and log; discard authority is limited to Section 5 item 8 junk-mail category.
  5. No opening or handling of parcels appearing to contain contraband, hazardous material, biological agent, or evidence of a crime. Such items are held unopened in the segregated file, photographed on the outside only, and reported to counsel and (where appropriate) law enforcement per counsel's direction.
  6. No commingling. Principal's mail is held separately from Agent's personal or business mail.
  7. No sale, transfer, or disclosure of the Principal's mailing address or the contents of any received mail to any third party. Data-broker sale, marketing-list resale, and comparable disposition are prohibited.
  8. No compensation to the Agent for services under this Direction. The Agent serves without fee; reasonable out-of-pocket costs (postage, scanner supplies, certified-mail fees, secure storage) are reimbursable from Principal's segregated proceeds account per Instrument 10 § 7 if funds exist, otherwise carried at Agent's cost.

Every physical original held under this Direction is filed in a segregated, locked, fire-resistant enclosure at the Agent's business address of record (DanDurand Enterprises, Inc., 1915 Highway 36 West, PMB 140, Roseville, Minnesota 55113), indexed by sender + received date + Dossier scan filename. A written mail-handling ledger is maintained and made available to the Principal on request and to counsel of record on request; the ledger is delivered to the Principal on release and on any revocation of this Direction. A notarized copy of the Principal's photo identification is attached to Instrument 1 and may be presented in conjunction with this Direction.

10 · Duration and Revocation

This Direction is effective on execution and remains effective until (a) revoked in writing by the Principal, (b) the Principal's release from pretrial custody with a thirty (30) day transition window for orderly return of held originals and the mail-handling ledger, or (c) the Principal's execution of a successor Direction naming a successor Mail Agent. Revocation is not effective as to any custodian, post office, or courier until written notice of revocation has been received by that custodian. On revocation, the Agent surrenders all held originals, all scans, the complete mail-handling ledger, and any accrued reimbursement claim to the Principal or the successor Mail Agent.

Purpose of This Declaration

This is a sworn declaration by the true and lawful owner of the canine known as Gunner that (a) I have never sold, given, surrendered, transferred, abandoned, or authorized any transfer of ownership of Gunner to any person or entity; (b) any writing bearing my name that purports to authorize such a transfer is either forged or was executed by a person without authority to act for me; (c) I retain full and continuous legal title to Gunner and demand his prompt return to me or to my authorized Agent; and (d) any further transfer, adoption, sterilization, or disposition of Gunner without my written consent is unauthorized and may expose the transferor and the recipient to civil and criminal liability under Texas law.

Declaration

STATE OF TEXAS

COUNTY OF TRAVIS

Before me, the undersigned notary public, on this day personally appeared Kyle Scott Harris, who being duly sworn upon his oath, deposed and stated as follows:

1. My name is Kyle Scott Harris. I am over the age of eighteen, of sound mind, competent to make this declaration, and I have personal knowledge of the facts stated herein and they are true and correct.
2. I am currently in continuous pretrial custody at the Travis County Correctional Complex in Del Valle, Texas. My custody has been continuous throughout the period during which the events described in this declaration occurred.
3. I am the true, lawful, and continuous owner of a living male domesticated canine known as Gunner. I acquired Gunner prior to my incarceration. Gunner has been a member of my household since I acquired him.
4. Under the law of the State of Texas, a dog is personal property — chattel — belonging to its owner. Bueckner v. Hamel, 886 S.W.2d 368, 370 (Tex. App. — Houston [1st Dist.] 1994, writ denied). My title to Gunner is the same character of interest that Texas recognizes in any other item of personal property owned by an adult resident of the State.
5. I have never sold Gunner to any person or entity.
6. I have never given Gunner away to any person or entity.
7. I have never surrendered Gunner to any animal shelter, animal-services agency, rescue organization, humane society, or governmental body.
8. I have never signed any surrender form, release form, transfer form, adoption form, or other writing that authorizes or purports to authorize the transfer of ownership of Gunner to any person or entity.
9. I have never abandoned Gunner. During my incarceration Gunner was in the physical vicinity of my last pre-incarceration residence, in the constructive care of a person or persons who were present at that residence, and my expectation was that Gunner would remain there until I could arrange for his continued care or until I could return.
10. I have never appointed Bobbi Jo Rice — or any other person — as my agent, bailee, or attorney-in-fact for the purpose of transferring, surrendering, or disposing of Gunner. To the extent that any person has claimed to Collin County Animal Services or to any other party to hold that authority for me, that claim is false. Any writing that person may have signed purporting to transfer or surrender Gunner is either forged as to my signature or executed by a person without authority to act for me. Bobbi Jo Rice was a person with whom I had a domestic relationship prior to my incarceration; that relationship did not confer any legal authority upon her to convey my personal property.
11. I received no notice from Collin County Animal Services, from any adopter, from any veterinarian, from any peace officer, or from any other person that Gunner was in the custody of an animal shelter or animal-services agency. I received no notice that a holding period was running. I received no notice that adoption was being considered or arranged. I received no notice that Gunner had in fact been adopted, transferred, or placed in the possession of any third party.
12. Had I been given any such notice, I would have exercised every available means to redeem Gunner, to arrange care for Gunner with a friend or family member of my choosing, to communicate with the animal-services agency, to communicate with counsel, or to take any other lawful step to protect my ownership interest.
13. I understand and I am informed that Texas law imposes minimum holding periods on stray animals held by shelters before disposition. See Tex. Health & Safety Code § 823.003 (shelter operating standards); § 826.033 (holding periods for impounded dogs and cats). I have never received any documentation that would establish that any such holding period was observed as to Gunner or that the statutory notice-and-opportunity provisions were satisfied as to me as the true owner.
14. I hereby declare that I retain full, continuous, and unbroken legal title to Gunner as of the date of this declaration. No adoption, transfer, or purported change of ownership executed during my incarceration is authorized or lawful as to me.
15. I hereby demand that Gunner be returned to me or to my authorized Agent Troy DanDurand at the earliest lawful date. Delivery to my Agent shall be treated as delivery to me for all purposes.
16. I hereby give express notice to any adopter, foster, rescue partner, or other person presently in possession of Gunner that (a) I am the true owner of Gunner; (b) any transfer of Gunner to that person was unauthorized; (c) that person's continued possession of Gunner without my consent is a continuing conversion of my personal property under Texas law; and (d) any good-faith-purchaser defense such person may seek to assert is defeated as of the date such person receives this notice.
17. I hereby give express notice to any veterinarian or veterinary hospital that has treated or is presently treating Gunner that (a) I am the true and lawful owner of Gunner as of the date of this declaration; (b) I preserve for evidentiary purposes the entirety of Gunner's veterinary record, chart, imaging, laboratory work, and communications with any person purporting to be Gunner's owner during the period of my incarceration; and (c) I demand that no non-emergency medical procedure — including but not limited to sterilization, elective surgery, or euthanasia — be performed on Gunner without my written consent or the written consent of my authorized Agent Troy DanDurand.
18. I hereby give express notice to Collin County Animal Services that (a) I am the true owner of Gunner; (b) any intake record that identifies any person other than me as Gunner's owner is either inaccurate as a matter of fact or was created upon the false representation of a person without authority to convey my property; (c) I preserve for evidentiary purposes all intake documentation, holding-period documentation, notice documentation, microchip-scan documentation, surrender documentation, adoption documentation, veterinary-triage documentation, kennel-card documentation, photographic and video documentation, and any related paper or electronic record concerning Gunner; and (d) I direct Collin County Animal Services to preserve all such records for the pendency of any civil, criminal, or administrative proceeding arising from Gunner's intake and disposition.
19. I reserve all civil, administrative, and criminal remedies available to me under Texas and federal law, including but not limited to: recovery of the chattel; damages for the reasonable value of the chattel plus special sentimental value where permitted by law; damages for the loss of use of the chattel; exemplary damages for conversion committed knowingly or with reckless disregard for my rights; damages for mental anguish where recoverable; injunctive relief prohibiting further transfer, sterilization, or disposition of Gunner without my consent; and — where the elements are met — referral to law enforcement for evaluation of theft of chattel under Tex. Penal Code § 31.03 and any related offense under Texas Penal Code Chapters 31, 32, 37, and 42.
20. I authorize Troy DanDurand — my Agent under the Statutory Durable Power of Attorney and Limited Power of Attorney included in Package DPOA-KH-20260903 — to receive Gunner on my behalf; to sign any receipt or release required to accomplish return of Gunner; to communicate with any party concerning Gunner's return and Gunner's care; and to take any other lawful step in furtherance of this declaration.
21. I execute this declaration freely and voluntarily, in the presence of the notary public whose seal and signature appear below.

Declaration

Instrument: #4 — Reclamation Demand (Gunner)

1 · Purpose of This Demand

This document is a formal demand for the return of personal chattel — the dog Gunner — to his lawful owner, Kyle Scott Harris, or to his attorney-in-fact of record, Troy DanDurand. This demand incorporates by reference the Declaration of Ownership — Gunner and the Texas Statutory Durable Power of Attorney executed by Kyle Scott Harris on 2026-09-03.

As of receipt of this demand, each recipient is on actual notice of Kyle Scott Harris's continuing and undisputed ownership of Gunner, and of the fact that any prior transfer, adoption, purported surrender, or purported release of Gunner was executed without the knowledge, consent, authorization, or agency of Kyle Scott Harris.

2 · Legal Basis

  • Conversion doctrine. Texas common-law conversion — wrongful exercise of dominion or control over the personal property of another to the exclusion of, or inconsistent with, the owner's rights. See Waisath v. Lack's Stores, Inc., 474 S.W.2d 444 (Tex. 1971); Green Int'l, Inc. v. Solis, 951 S.W.2d 384 (Tex. 1997).
  • Refusal after demand is the conversion. Where possession was originally lawful, refusal to return the property after demand by the true owner completes the tort of conversion. See Presley v. Cooper, 284 S.W.2d 138 (Tex. 1955).
  • Property interest in companion animals. Bueckner v. Hamel, 886 S.W.2d 368 (Tex. App. — Houston [1st Dist.] 1994, writ denied).
  • Theft by appropriation. Texas Penal Code § 31.03 — unlawful appropriation of property with intent to deprive the owner, including retention of property known to be another's after demand.
  • Shelter operating standards. Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 823 and Section 826.033 (mandatory holding period).
  • Fourteenth Amendment due process as enforced through 42 U.S.C. § 1983 (deprivation of property without notice or hearing).
  • Good-faith-purchaser doctrine limitation. A purported adopter, transferee, or subsequent possessor cannot acquire greater title than the transferor possessed; a shelter that never held valid title cannot convey valid title. Once actual notice of the true owner's claim is received, any good-faith-purchaser posture is extinguished as to future retention.

4 · Formal Demand for Return

DEMAND

Kyle Scott Harris, as lawful and continuous owner of the dog Gunner, hereby demands the return of Gunner to his attorney-in-fact of record, Troy DanDurand, within ten (10) business days of receipt of this instrument.

Return shall be effected by physical delivery of Gunner to the attorney-in-fact at a mutually convenient location within the State of Texas, or, at the recipient's election, by the attorney-in-fact taking custody at a location designated by the recipient upon reasonable advance notice.

5 · Terms of Return

  1. Return shall be to the attorney-in-fact Troy DanDurand personally, or to a written designee bearing a written authorization signed by the attorney-in-fact.
  2. Gunner shall be returned in the same physical condition as most recently observed, with all veterinary records, vaccination records, medical records, microchip transfer paperwork, licensing paperwork, and any accompanying tags, collar, or identification transferred simultaneously.
  3. The attorney-in-fact shall provide a written receipt at the point of transfer, identifying Gunner and the date and time of return.
  4. Any veterinary care, boarding, or reasonable custodial expense incurred by the current possessor after receipt of this demand shall not be a condition of return; any such claim shall be addressed separately, without lien on the animal.
  5. No release of claims, waiver, non-disparagement clause, or confidentiality clause shall be a condition of return. Return of chattel is not a settlement.

6 · Extinguishment of Good-Faith-Purchaser Defense

Any purported adopter, foster, transferee, or subsequent possessor of Gunner may have taken possession without knowledge of the defect in the chain of title. That posture, whatever its merit prior to this notice, is extinguished as of receipt of this instrument. Continued retention of Gunner after receipt of this notice constitutes knowing exercise of dominion and control over the personal property of another and completes the elements of civil conversion and, upon appropriate showing, Texas Penal Code § 31.03 theft by appropriation.

7 · Preservation Duty During Pendency

Pending return, the current possessor and CCAS shall preserve Gunner's health, safety, and identifying information. No non-emergency medical procedure, no elective surgery, no cosmetic alteration, no chip removal, no chip reprogramming, no transfer of registration, no re-homing, no transfer of possession to any third party, and no destruction of any accompanying record shall occur absent written consent of Kyle Scott Harris or his attorney-in-fact. Emergency veterinary care to preserve life or prevent suffering shall be permitted and documented, with notice to the attorney-in-fact within twenty-four (24) hours of any such intervention.

8 · Prohibited Actions After Receipt

DO NOT — PROHIBITED AFTER RECEIPT

  • Do not treat this demand as adversarial correspondence requiring response through counsel only. Return of chattel is the immediate remedy; counsel exchange, if any, follows return.

Failure to return Gunner within ten (10) business days of receipt of this demand may result in, without limitation:

Instrument: #5 — Preservation Letter (Nebula)

1 · Purpose of This Letter

This document is a formal litigation-hold and evidence-preservation notice concerning the dog Nebula, personal chattel of Kyle Scott Harris. It is issued in anticipation of civil, administrative, and criminal proceedings arising from Nebula's intake, holding, and euthanasia. This notice operates in tandem with, and is expressly incorporated by reference into, the Declaration of Ownership — Nebula executed by Kyle Scott Harris of even date (2026-09-03).

As of receipt of this letter, each recipient is on actual notice of a duty to preserve every item, record, sample, tissue, digital record, and communication described in this instrument. Destruction, discard, overwriting, deletion, alteration, or routine-cycle disposal of any preserved item after receipt of this notice may constitute spoliation of evidence and may give rise to independent civil, administrative, and criminal exposure separate from the underlying claims.

2 · Legal Basis for the Preservation Duty

  • Common-law duty to preserve evidence when litigation is reasonably anticipated. See Trevino v. Ortega, 969 S.W.2d 950 (Tex. 1998); Brookshire Bros., Ltd. v. Aldridge, 438 S.W.3d 9 (Tex. 2014); Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. v. Johnson, 106 S.W.3d 718 (Tex. 2003).
  • Rule of completeness. Texas Rule of Evidence 107.
  • Tampering with governmental records. Texas Penal Code § 37.10.
  • Abuse of official capacity · Official oppression. Texas Penal Code §§ 39.02, 39.03.
  • Cruelty to non-livestock animals. Texas Penal Code § 42.092.
  • Shelter operating standards. Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 823 and Section 826.033 (mandatory holding period).
  • Rabies control record retention. Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 826 and Texas Administrative Code Title 25, Chapter 169.
  • Property interest in companion animals. Bueckner v. Hamel, 886 S.W.2d 368 (Tex. App. — Houston [1st Dist.] 1994, writ denied).
  • Fourteenth Amendment due process as enforced through 42 U.S.C. § 1983 (deprivation of property without notice or hearing).
  • Federal spoliation instruction available in § 1983 actions per Silvestri v. Gen. Motors Corp., 271 F.3d 583 (4th Cir. 2001) (persuasive).

  • Property interest in companion animals. Bueckner v. Hamel, 886 S.W.2d 368 (Tex. App. — Houston [1st Dist.] 1994, writ denied).
  • Fourteenth Amendment due process as enforced through 42 U.S.C. § 1983 (deprivation of property without notice or hearing).

21. Instrument 18 — Rescission of Purported Surrender (Bobbi Jo Rice)
ProphetFuel™ AiOS  |  ZeroPoint PureLogic™
Sworn Rescission — Any Purported Surrender
Gunner & Nebula — Void ab initio as to Bobbi Jo Rice · Any Other Signatory · Any Agency Claim
Declarant / Owner: Kyle Scott Harris
Attorney-in-Fact: Troy DanDurand
Current Custody of Declarant: Travis County Correctional Complex
Underlying Criminal Cause: D-1-DC-25-303689

Instrument: #3 — Rescission of Purported Surrender

1 · Purpose of This Instrument

This document is a sworn rescission and repudiation of any and every purported surrender, release, transfer, disposition, adoption authorization, or euthanasia authorization form — whether now in existence or later discovered — that concerns the dog Gunner or the dog Nebula and that purports to have been executed by Bobbi Jo Rice or by any other person or entity claiming to act as owner or agent of the owner. This instrument incorporates by reference the Declarations of Ownership — Gunner and Nebula and the Texas Statutory Durable Power of Attorney executed by Kyle Scott Harris on 2026-09-03.

As of receipt of this instrument, each recipient is on actual notice that any such surrender or authorization form is void ab initio, was executed without the knowledge, consent, authorization, or agency of Kyle Scott Harris, was never subsequently ratified by Kyle Scott Harris, and confers no title, no possessory right, and no defense to any downstream transferee.

2 · Legal Basis

  • Agency principle — no authority, no conveyance. A person who is not the owner and not the owner's authorized agent cannot convey title, surrender custody, or authorize destruction of another's chattel. See Douglass v. Panama, Inc., 504 S.W.2d 776 (Tex. 1974); Restatement (Third) of Agency § 6.01.
  • Void ab initio. An instrument executed without authority is void from the outset, not merely voidable; it cannot be cured by subsequent good-faith reliance of third parties.
  • No ratification. The owner has taken no action — verbal, written, or by conduct — that could constitute ratification of the unauthorized act, and by this instrument expressly and formally rejects and repudiates any such act.
  • Property interest in companion animals. Bueckner v. Hamel, 886 S.W.2d 368 (Tex. App. — Houston [1st Dist.] 1994, writ denied).
  • Forgery. Texas Penal Code § 32.21 — unauthorized signing of another's name to a writing purporting to be another's act, with intent to defraud or harm.
  • Tampering with governmental record. Texas Penal Code § 37.10 — where the surrender or adoption paperwork becomes part of a governmental record.
  • Tampering with or fabricating physical evidence. Texas Penal Code § 37.09 — where the record is created with knowledge of pending or contemplated investigation.
  • Theft. Texas Penal Code § 31.03 — unlawful appropriation of property with intent to deprive the owner, including procurement of transfer by deception or false representation of authority.
  • Fourteenth Amendment due process as enforced through 42 U.S.C. § 1983 — a state agency that accepts and acts upon a facially unauthorized surrender without independent verification of authority deprives the true owner of property without notice or hearing.

3 · Recipients of This Rescission

Primary — Collin County Animal Services [CCAS]

4 · Sworn Statements of Kyle Scott Harris

¶ 1. I, Kyle Scott Harris, am the lawful and continuous owner of the dog Gunner and was the lawful and continuous owner of the dog Nebula, up to and including the date of Nebula's death.
¶ 2. I have never sold, gifted, given, surrendered, transferred, released, or otherwise conveyed either Gunner or Nebula to Collin County Animal Services, to any other shelter, to any adopter, to any veterinarian, to any rescue organization, or to any other person or entity.
¶ 3. I have never signed any surrender form, release form, transfer form, adoption authorization, disposition authorization, or euthanasia authorization concerning Gunner or Nebula.
¶ 4. I have never authorized Bobbi Jo Rice, orally, in writing, by conduct, or by any other means, to surrender, transfer, release, dispose of, adopt out, euthanize, sign any authorization form concerning, or in any other way exercise ownership rights over Gunner or Nebula.
¶ 5. I have never authorized any other person or entity, orally, in writing, by conduct, or by any other means, to surrender, transfer, release, dispose of, adopt out, euthanize, sign any authorization form concerning, or in any other way exercise ownership rights over Gunner or Nebula.
¶ 6. Bobbi Jo Rice was never appointed as my agent, attorney-in-fact, bailee, keeper, custodian, or fiduciary as to Gunner or Nebula. Any characterization of Bobbi Jo Rice as owner, co-owner, agent, or authorized representative in any surrender or adoption record is false.
¶ 7. 5 · Formal Rescission

RESCISSION — VOID AB INITIO

Pursuant to the sworn statements above, and to the extent any such instrument exists or may hereafter be discovered, every purported surrender form, release form, transfer form, adoption authorization, disposition authorization, or euthanasia authorization concerning Gunner or Nebula that purports to bear the signature of Bobbi Jo Rice, or of any other person or entity claiming to act as owner or authorized agent of the owner, is hereby RESCINDED, REPUDIATED, AND DECLARED VOID AB INITIO.

Eligibility Gate — Read Before Filing

Statutory Eligibility Under 50 U.S.C. § 3911

The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act [SCRA] applies to a "servicemember," defined at 50 U.S.C. § 3911(1) as: (a) a member of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force, or Coast Guard on active duty as defined by 10 U.S.C. § 101(d)(1); (b) a member of the National Guard called to active service by the President or the Secretary of Defense under 32 U.S.C. § 502(f) for a period of more than thirty consecutive days; or (c) a commissioned officer of the Public Health Service or the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration in active service.

The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act does not apply to veterans who are not currently in active status, except with respect to certain limited post-separation tails including the 90-day window under 50 U.S.C. § 3937(a)(2) (interest-rate cap on pre-service obligations).

File this instrument only if Kyle Scott Harris was on active duty on the date the underlying civil obligation matured or is presently on active duty for purposes of § 3931 default-judgment protection. If Kyle is a veteran-only (no current active-duty status and no active-duty status during the operative period), route instead to the veteran-track fallback described in Part D of this package (Veterans Treatment Court screening + character-evidence mitigation) rather than filing this instrument.

Important Legal Boundaries

What SCRA Does and Does Not Do Here
  • Applies to civil actions and proceedings. The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act stays or otherwise protects civil actions in which the Servicemember is a party. 50 U.S.C. § 3931 (default judgments); § 3932 (stay of proceedings); § 3934 (stay of execution of judgments and attachments).
  • Does not stay criminal prosecution. The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act does not stay the underlying criminal cases pending against Kyle Scott Harris in Travis County and Collin County. Criminal-defense strategy in those cases continues through court-appointed counsel of record.
  • Financial protections. The 6% interest-rate cap under 50 U.S.C. § 3937 applies to pre-service financial obligations upon written notice to the creditor.
  • Housing and vehicle-lease protections. §§ 3951–3955 govern lease terminations upon qualifying orders. These provisions typically require entry onto active duty or receipt of qualifying deployment/permanent-change-of-station orders and are unlikely to apply to a pretrial detainee whose separation from ordinary life is caused by state criminal charges rather than by military orders.
  • Default-judgment protection. § 3931 applies whenever the Servicemember has not made an appearance in a civil action; the court is required to appoint counsel or grant a minimum ninety-day stay upon proof of service.

Notice. Kyle Scott Harris is a servicemember within the meaning of the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act of 2003, 50 U.S.C. §§ 3901–4043, on the basis of the service history stated in the caption above. Kyle Scott Harris is presently unable to appear personally in civil proceedings, to negotiate directly with creditors, or to conduct in-person financial affairs due to continuous pretrial detention in Travis County, Texas.

The following statutory protections are hereby invoked without waiver:

1. Default-Judgment Protection. 50 U.S.C. § 3931. No default judgment may be entered against the Servicemember in any civil action or proceeding without compliance with the affidavit-and-appointment-of-counsel provisions of § 3931(b). Any court considering a request for default judgment against Kyle Scott Harris is directed to this Notice.
2. Stay of Proceedings. 50 U.S.C. § 3932. The Servicemember reserves the right to seek a stay of proceedings of not less than ninety days in any pending civil action, pursuant to § 3932(b), on the ground that his military service materially affects his ability to appear, participate, and defend.
3. Interest-Rate Cap. 50 U.S.C. § 3937. Written notice is hereby given to every holder of a pre-service financial obligation of Kyle Scott Harris that the annual interest rate on that obligation is capped at six percent (6%) for the period of military service and, for mortgages and trust deeds, for one year thereafter, as provided by § 3937(a)(1)–(2). A copy of the Servicemember's DD Form 214 or of orders establishing active-duty status is available upon written request to the Agent identified above.
4. Stay of Enforcement of Judgments and Attachments. 50 U.S.C. § 3934. The Servicemember reserves the right to seek a stay or vacation of any judgment, execution, attachment, or garnishment obtained during or within thirty days after the period of military service, on the ground that his ability to comply is materially affected by military service.
5. Foreclosure and Repossession Protection. 50 U.S.C. §§ 3952, 3953, 3958. The Servicemember invokes the mortgage, installment-contract, and residential-lease protections of these sections with respect to any pre-service obligation.
6. No Waiver. Nothing in this Notice constitutes an appearance in any pending civil action, submission to any court's personal jurisdiction, or waiver of any right or defense — including but not limited to the rights described above and any statute-of-limitations, service-of-process, jurisdictional, or substantive defense.
7. Direct Communication to Agent. Direct correspondence to the Servicemember at the Travis County Correctional Complex is permissible but may be delayed by facility mail-processing timelines; the Agent's channel is faster and equally authorized.

Section 3931(b)(1) requires that before entering judgment against a servicemember who has not made an appearance, the court shall require the plaintiff to file an affidavit stating whether or not the defendant is in military service and showing the necessary facts to support the affidavit. If the plaintiff cannot determine whether or not the defendant is in military service, the plaintiff shall file an affidavit stating that the plaintiff is unable to determine.
3. Section 3931(b)(2) requires that if the defendant is in military service, the court shall not enter a judgment until after appointing an attorney to represent the defendant.
4. Section 3931(d) requires that in any action covered by this section in which the defendant is in military service, the court shall grant a stay of proceedings for a minimum period of ninety (90) days upon application of counsel appointed under paragraph (2), or upon the court's own motion, if there may be a defense to the action that cannot be presented without the presence of the defendant.

Veterans Treatment Court Screening
