STATE OF TEXAS

COUNTY OF TRAVIS

Before me, the undersigned notary public, on this day personally appeared Kyle Scott Harris, who being duly sworn upon his oath, deposed and stated as follows:

1. My name is Kyle Scott Harris. I am over the age of eighteen, of sound mind, competent to make this affidavit, and I have personal knowledge of the facts stated herein and they are true and correct.
2. I am currently in continuous pretrial custody at the Travis County Correctional Complex in Del Valle, Texas. My custody in Travis and Collin County jails has been continuous throughout the period relevant to the matters described in this affidavit.
3. I am the lawful owner of two domesticated dogs: Nebula and Gunner. I acquired and cared for both dogs prior to my incarceration. I have never sold, given, surrendered, or transferred ownership of either dog to any person or entity, including but not limited to Bobbi Jo, Collin County Animal Services, or any adopter.
4. Prior to my incarceration, I had a domestic relationship with Bobbi Jo. During and after that relationship, Bobbi Jo had access to my home and to my personal property, including the two dogs, by virtue of that relationship. Bobbi Jo was never my authorized agent or bailee for the purpose of transferring, surrendering, or disposing of the dogs.
5. The pending criminal cases against me identified in the caption above rest in whole or in part on statements made by Bobbi Jo to law enforcement. I have been informed and I believe that Bobbi Jo has since recanted material portions of those statements. I did not commit the offenses alleged against me by Bobbi Jo.
6. While I have been incarcerated, my dog Nebula was euthanized at a Collin County animal-services facility. I did not consent to Nebula's euthanasia. I was not given notice by anyone — not by Bobbi Jo, not by Collin County Animal Services, not by any peace officer — that Nebula was in custody at an animal shelter, that a holding period was running, or that euthanasia was being considered or scheduled. I had no opportunity to redeem Nebula, arrange care for Nebula, transfer Nebula to a friend or family member, or otherwise intervene.
7. While I have been incarcerated, my dog Gunner was surrendered and adopted out through the same or a related process. I did not consent to Gunner's surrender or transfer. I was not given notice of the surrender or of the adoption. I had no opportunity to redeem Gunner or arrange alternative care.
8. The loss of Nebula's life and the loss of possession of Gunner have caused me serious and continuing personal, emotional, and economic harm. Both dogs were members of my household. I loved them and cared for them and would have taken every step available to me to protect them had I been given any notice or opportunity.

In Collin County my court-appointed counsel is an attorney I know as John B. "Brad". 10. My requests have gone unanswered or have been met with responses that did not result in any filings. I do not know of any strategic reason why the motions listed in the 12-Motion Gap Audit were not filed. As I understand it, none of those motions requires a hearing before it is filed, and none carries a downside to me if filed.
11. Part II — Statement of Facts

The following facts are stated on the personal knowledge of complainant Troy DanDurand where noted, and on information and belief drawn from (i) recorded telephone communications with Kyle Scott Harris from the Travis County Correctional Complex on and after August 17, 2026 (forty-six calls transcribed and catalogued), (ii) documentary evidence catalogued in Part V, (iii) Short Message Service communications between Ms. Rice and Ms. Martin, and (iv) publicly available third-party publications identified with source anchors. Where a fact is stated on information and belief, complainant identifies the source and expressly reserves the right to supplement upon receipt of confirmatory records.

Fact 1 — Ownership of the canines "Nebula" and "Gunner." At all times material to this Complaint, Kyle Scott Harris was the sole registered owner of two canines known as "Nebula" and "Gunner." Ownership is documented by veterinary records to be produced from Mr. Harris's veterinarian, by microchip registry lookup pending, and by photographs and correspondence produced by Mr. Harris. Under Texas law, a companion animal is the personal property of its registered owner. See Texas Health and Safety Code Chapter 823; Texas Penal Code Section 31.01(5).
Fact 2 — Cohabitation and separation. Ms. Rice and Mr. Harris cohabited at 5900 County Road 277, Apartment 222, Melissa, Texas 75454 (Collin County) until their separation on or about a date to be confirmed by supplemental affidavit. Ms. Rice was not the registered owner of either canine, was not identified on the veterinary records as owner, and was not listed on any microchip registry as owner.
Fact 3 — Removal of the canines. On a date on or about November 26, 2025, Ms. Rice, without the consent, knowledge, or authorization of Mr. Harris, removed the canines "Nebula" and "Gunner" from the Melissa apartment. Mr. Harris was incarcerated at the Travis County Correctional Complex at the time of the removal and had no means of preventing it. Mr. Harris transmitted a Short Message Service request for the return of his animals; Ms. Rice refused and concealed the name of the shelter to which she had surrendered them.
Fact 4 — Surrender to Collin County Animal Services. On or about November 26, 2025, Ms. Rice presented the canines "Nebula" and "Gunner" to Collin County Animal Services, 4750 Community Avenue, McKinney, Texas 75071, and executed one or more surrender documents. On information and belief, in the course of executing those documents, Ms. Rice represented herself as the owner of, or as a person authorized to surrender, the canines — a representation that was false when made, was made with the intent to induce Collin County Animal Services to accept the animals, and did in fact induce Collin County Animal Services to effect their disposition. Beth Martin, Mr. Harris's mother, subsequently telephoned Collin County Animal Services, identified herself as the mother of the true owner Kyle Scott Harris, and stated to the intake worker that Bobbi Jo Rice was not the owner. Collin County Animal Services personnel refused to honor Ms. Martin as the true-owner designee. That refusal, and any communications memorializing it, are material and are the subject of the records-preservation request identified in the Cover Letter.
Fact 5 — Disposition of the canines. On information and belief, "Nebula" was euthanized and "Gunner" was adopted out to a third party. Confirmation is pending production of records under the Texas Public Information Act, Texas Government Code Chapter 552. The selection of Nebula — the canine that provided the most effective post-traumatic-stress support to Mr. Harris — for euthanasia, contrasted with the adoption of Gunner, is not consistent with a random or standard intake process. That selective outcome is a fact from which malice may be inferred at trial. If Ms. Rice communicated any preference, designation, or characterization of the animals to Collin County Animal Services personnel that influenced disposition, the offense catalogued in Part III, subsection C (Cruelty to Non-Livestock Animals under Texas Penal Code Section 42.092) is engaged in its aggravated form.
Fact 6 — The Short Message Service recantation admission by Ms. Rice. On a date on or about November 8, 2025, Ms. Rice transmitted a Short Message Service communication to Beth Martin (Mr. Harris's mother) stating in substance: "I sent an email to the District Attorney stating that this never happened." The "this" referred to is the alleged Travis County offense that is the subject of cause D-1-DC-25-303689 and companion misdemeanor causes. This admission constitutes (i) evidence of a prior inconsistent statement by the State's principal witness, discoverable under Texas Rule of Evidence 613, (ii) impeachment material under Rule 608, (iii) evidence bearing on Ms. Rice's credibility discoverable under the Michael Morton Act, Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 39.14, and (iv) Brady/Giglio material subject to disclosure by any prosecutor with actual or constructive knowledge of it. The email referenced by Ms. Rice, and all Travis County District Attorney inbound-email logs for the relevant window, are the subject of a separate preservation demand catalogued in Part V.

Contradiction Cluster — Bobbi Jo Rice (Preservation-Critical)

(a) Public claim (Spectrum News, on or about March 29, 2025): "head chef at the Waldorf Astoria." Third-party inquiry return: no record. (b) Short Message Service to Beth Martin (November 8, 2025): "I sent an email to the DA stating that this never happened." (c) Short Message Service to Beth Martin: "I will testify on his behalf to his innocence." (d) Short Message Service to Beth Martin: "You can call the shelter where he was rescued … it's probably too late … now that he's with a proper rescue." (e) Short Message Service to Beth Martin: "I have the video you sent me but no number." Each of the foregoing is inconsistent with (i) the sworn or unsworn statements Ms. Rice made to peace officers on or about September 6, 2025, that resulted in Mr. Harris's arrest, and (ii) any position Ms. Rice may take at trial. Each is material to the pending prosecutions and to the offenses charged in Part III.

Fact 7 — The tampered recording. A video recording of an interview or segment involving Ms. Rice and Mr. Boatwright, together with related derivative recordings distributed on Facebook and other platforms, appears to have been altered in a manner that removed content adverse to Ms. Rice's stated positions. The tampered file, contrast recordings, cryptographic hash values (Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit), and diarization analysis are catalogued in Part V. Part III — Statute Map and Element Analysis

For each offense listed below, the elements of the statute are mapped to the specific facts alleged in Part II.

A. Texas Penal Code Section 31.03 — Theft

"A person commits an offense if he unlawfully appropriates property with intent to deprive the owner of property."

  • Appropriation — Removal of Nebula and Gunner from the Melissa apartment (Fact 3) and surrender to Collin County Animal Services (Fact 4) is appropriation of property under Section 31.01(4).
  • Unlawful — Appropriation was without the effective consent of the owner (Section 31.01(3)); Ms. Rice was neither the registered owner nor an authorized agent (Facts 1, 2).
  • Intent to deprive — Surrender to Animal Services with disposition authority constitutes intent to withhold the property from the owner permanently or for so extended a period that a major portion of the value or enjoyment is lost (Section 31.01(2)(A)).
  • Grade — Depending on fair market value or replacement cost of the animals and any aggravating factors (Section 31.03(e)), the offense grade may range from Class C misdemeanor to state jail felony.

B. Texas Penal Code Section 32.46 — Fraudulent Securing of Document Execution

"A person commits an offense if, with intent to defraud or harm any person, he, by deception . . . causes another to sign or execute any document affecting property or service or the pecuniary interest of any person . . . ."

  • Deception — Ms. Rice's presentation of herself as an authorized surrenderer (Fact 4) satisfies Section 31.01(1)(A): "creating or confirming by words or conduct a false impression of law or fact that is likely to affect the judgment of another in the transaction."
  • Causes another to sign or execute a document — The intake form, surrender form, or disposition authorization executed by Collin County Animal Services personnel on the basis of Ms. Rice's representation.
  • Affecting property — The property affected is the canines and the ownership interest of Mr. Harris.
  • Intent to defraud or harm — Directed at Mr. Harris, whose ownership interest was extinguished or impaired by the fraudulent surrender.
  • Grade — Section 32.46 grades this offense from Class C misdemeanor to first-degree felony, dependent on value and aggravating factors.

C. Texas Penal Code Section 42.092 — Cruelty to Non-Livestock Animals

"A person commits an offense if the person intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly . . . (2) without the owner's effective consent, kills, administers poison to, or causes serious bodily injury to an animal . . . ."

  • Actus reus — If Nebula was euthanized as a proximate consequence of Ms. Rice's fraudulent surrender (Fact 5), Section 42.092(b)(2) is engaged. Ms. Rice "cause[d]" the killing within the meaning of the statute by initiating the causal chain via her fraudulent representation to the shelter.
  • Mens rea — At minimum, recklessness: awareness of and conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk that surrendering an owned animal to a public shelter as an unowned or unauthorized surrender would result in euthanasia. Where Ms. Rice selected Nebula (the therapy dog) for the surrender-that-leads-to-euthanasia and Gunner for the surrender-that-leads-to-adoption, specific-intent malice may be inferred.
  • Without owner's effective consent — Mr. Harris did not consent (Facts 1, 3, 4).
  • Grade — Section 42.092(c)(1)-(2) grades the offense as a state jail felony or third-degree felony, depending on whether the conduct killed the animal.

D. Texas Penal Code Section 37.09 — Tampering With or Fabricating Physical Evidence

"A person commits an offense if, knowing that an investigation or official proceeding is pending or in progress, he . . . (1) alters, destroys, or conceals any record, document, or thing with intent to impair its verity, legibility, or availability as evidence in the investigation or official proceeding."

  • Knowledge of pending or foreseeable investigation — Ms. Rice was the complaining witness in the September 6, 2025 Travis County incident and a chain-of-custody witness to felony matter cause 199-80678-2026. She had actual or constructive knowledge that recordings involving her would be evidence in pending or foreseeable proceedings.
  • Alteration — The recording described in Fact 7 was materially altered.
  • Intent — If Ms. Rice altered, directed the alteration of, or with knowledge published a knowingly altered recording, Section 37.09(a)(1) is engaged.
  • Grade — State jail felony under Section 37.09(c).

E. Texas Penal Code Section 37.08 — False Report to Peace Officer

"A person commits an offense if, with intent to deceive, he knowingly makes a false statement that is material to a criminal investigation and makes the statement to . . . a peace officer or federal special investigator conducting the investigation . . . ."

  • Statement to peace officer — Statements made by Ms. Rice to Austin Police Department officers, Travis County peace officers, or Collin County peace officers in the course of the investigation resulting in the accusations against Mr. Harris.
  • Materiality — A statement is material if it could have affected the course or outcome of the investigation. Ms. Rice's account of the events is at the core of the accusations against Mr. Harris; her statements are per se material.
  • Falsity — Established by comparison of Ms. Rice's law-enforcement statements against (i) her Short Message Service admission to Beth Martin that "this never happened" (Fact 6), (ii) prior inconsistent statements catalogued in the Contradiction Cluster, (iii) physical and documentary evidence catalogued in Part V, and (iv) testimony of independent witnesses.
  • Grade — Class B misdemeanor under Section 37.08(b).

F. Related Offenses Reserved for Consideration

  • Texas Penal Code Section 37.02 (Perjury) and Section 37.03 (Aggravated Perjury) — If Ms. Rice has made any false statement under oath in an official proceeding (protective-order hearing, grand jury, deposition, affidavit, application for arrest warrant, sworn complaint).
  • Texas Penal Code Section 37.10 (Tampering with Governmental Record) — If Ms. Rice's employment representation, address representation, ownership representation, or any other material representation was memorialized in a governmental record with knowledge of its falsity.
  • Texas Penal Code Section 36.05 (Tampering with Witness) — Reserved pending investigation of any communication by Ms. Rice, or by a person acting in concert with her, directed at any witness in the pending criminal cases with intent to influence testimony.
  • Texas Penal Code Section 7.02 (Party Liability) — Reserved as to any co-actor with Ms. Rice in any of the offenses catalogued above.

Troy DanDurand — friend, legal researcher, and duly authorized agent for the aggrieved lawful owner, Kyle Scott Harris, who is presently in continuous pretrial detention at the Travis County Correctional Complex.

Subject of Complaint

Facility: Collin County Animal Services, 4750 Community Avenue, McKinney, Texas 75071, telephone (972) 547-7292.

Conduct: During the aggrieved owner's continuous pretrial incarceration, his two dogs, Nebula and Gunner, came into the custody of Collin County Animal Services. Nebula was euthanized. Statutory and Regulatory Basis

The Texas Health and Safety Code Chapter 823 (Animal Shelters) sets minimum standards for shelter operations, including record-keeping, holding periods, disposition procedures, and euthanasia. The Texas Department of State Health Services adopts implementing rules and inspects shelters for compliance. Local ordinances in Collin County and the City of McKinney supplement these requirements.

On information and belief, the conduct described above breached the following categories of standards: (1) owner-identification and reasonable-notice requirements before disposition of an owned animal; (2) statutory holding period before euthanasia; (3) documentation and record-keeping for intake, disposition, and euthanasia authorization; (4) authority verification for third-party surrenders of owned animals.

Relief Sought

1 — Facility Inspection

Conduct an unannounced inspection of Collin County Animal Services with focus on intake documentation, holding-period compliance, owner-notice procedures, disposition authorization, and euthanasia records for the trailing twenty-four months.

2 — Records Preservation Order

Direct the facility to preserve all records relating to Nebula and Gunner pending resolution of this complaint and pending parallel criminal and civil proceedings.

3 — Investigation of Nebula Euthanasia

Investigate whether the euthanasia of Nebula complied with Chapter 823 and applicable rules regarding owner notice, holding period, and lawful basis for euthanasia.

4 — Investigation of Gunner Transfer

Investigate whether the surrender and subsequent adoption of Gunner was authorized by a person with lawful authority to convey the owner's property.

5 — Written Findings

Issue written findings to Complainant identifying each deviation from statute, rule, or local ordinance, and identifying the corrective action ordered.

6 — Referral

Refer any findings suggesting criminal conduct to the Collin County Sheriff and to the Collin County District Attorney (with request for special-prosecutor assignment given the concurrent conflict).

Preservation of Rights

This administrative complaint is filed in parallel with sworn criminal complaints filed with the Melissa Police Department and the Collin County Sheriff's Office, and does not waive any civil claim of the aggrieved owner.

Jurisdictional Basis

The State Commission on Judicial Conduct has authority under Article V, Section 1-a of the Texas Constitution and Chapter 33 of the Texas Government Code to receive and investigate complaints alleging violations of the Texas Code of Judicial Conduct. The conduct complained of falls within the Commission's jurisdiction and directly affects a person presently held in pretrial custody.

Statement of Facts

Fact 1 — Custody and Pretrial Posture

Kyle Scott Harris has been held in continuous pretrial detention across Travis County and Collin County jails throughout the material period. He is presently housed at the Travis County Correctional Complex. He has been at all material times represented by court-appointed counsel: Attorney Holub in Collin County and Attorney Brad [surname to confirm] in Travis County.

Fact 2 — Complaining Witness Recantation on the Record

The complaining witness in the underlying criminal proceedings, Bobbi Jo Rice, has recanted material portions of her sworn accusations against Kyle Scott Harris. The recantation is documented in the record maintained by Complainant and has been the subject of contemporaneous State Bar of Texas grievances filed against both defense attorneys of record and of sworn criminal complaints filed with the Melissa Police Department and the Collin County Sheriff's Office on 2026-09-03.

Fact 3 — Constitutionally Deficient Performance by Defense Counsel

An independent audit of the case docket (the "12-Motion Gap Audit," maintained in Complainant's Dossier) identifies approximately twelve categories of pretrial motions and orders that any competent defense counsel would have prepared and filed on the facts of this case. To Complainant's knowledge, neither Attorney Holub nor Attorney Brad [surname to confirm] has filed any substantive pretrial motion in either county, including but not limited to: motion to reduce or reconsider bond; Brady/Giglio production demand; Article 39.14 discovery motion (Michael Morton Act); motion for speedy trial; motion to suppress; motion in limine; motion to dismiss for insufficient evidence in light of recantation; motion for grand-jury minutes; motion to compel disclosure of exculpatory recantation; motion for expert funding; motion for continuance for investigation; and motion to appoint substitute counsel.

Fact 4 — Judicial Officer on Notice

The presiding judicial officer(s) have had constructive and, upon information and belief, actual notice of the failure of court-appointed counsel to file any substantive pretrial motions during a continuously extended pretrial detention. Docket entries, calendar calls, status conferences, and bond-review hearings during the material period reflect the absence of any defense filings and the continued incarceration of Kyle Scott Harris. Under United States v. Cronic, 466 U.S. 648 (1984), a court is required to inquire when defense counsel's total failure to subject the prosecution's case to meaningful adversarial testing raises a presumption of prejudice.

Fact 5 — Failure to Inquire, Substitute, or Otherwise Act

Notwithstanding the record described in Fact 4, upon information and belief the presiding judicial officer(s) did not: (a) sua sponte inquire on the record into the effectiveness of appointed counsel; (b) appoint substitute counsel or hold a hearing to consider substitution; (c) hold a hearing under Faretta v. California, 422 U.S. 806 (1975), to determine whether Kyle Scott Harris wished to proceed pro se or in hybrid representation given the vacuum; (d) address the recantation on the record or order its disclosure; (e) conduct a bond-review sua sponte given the length of pretrial detention and materially changed circumstances; or (f) take any action to remedy the constitutional deprivation.

Fact 6 — Failure to Report Attorney Misconduct

Canon 3D(2) of the Texas Code of Judicial Conduct requires that "a judge who receives information clearly establishing that a lawyer has committed a violation of the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct should take appropriate action." The complete non-filing of any substantive motion in a case involving a continuously incarcerated pretrial defendant, in the face of a documented complaining-witness recantation, raises a substantial question about the fitness of the lawyer(s) to practice law. Upon information and belief the presiding judicial officer(s) did not report the conduct of Attorney Holub or Attorney Brad [surname to confirm] to the State Bar of Texas Office of the Chief Disciplinary Counsel.

Fact 7 — Consequence to the Aggrieved Person

Kyle Scott Harris remains in pretrial custody as of the date of this complaint. His personal property, including two dogs identified as Nebula and Gunner, has been lost during his incarceration (Nebula euthanized at a Collin County animal-services facility; Gunner surrendered and adopted out). His constitutional rights under the Sixth Amendment (assistance of counsel), Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments (due process), and Eighth Amendment (excessive bail) have been implicated by the judicial inaction complained of herein.

Counts

Count 1 — Violation of Canon 2A — Failure to Comply with the Law and Promote Public Confidence in the Integrity of the Judiciary

Canon 2A: "A judge shall comply with the law and should act at all times in a manner that promotes public confidence in the integrity and impartiality of the judiciary."

Elements Alleged

By presiding over a continuously extended pretrial detention in which court-appointed defense counsel filed no substantive motion of any kind, and by failing to take corrective judicial action, the presiding judicial officer(s) failed to comply with binding constitutional law (Sixth Amendment right to effective assistance of counsel) and undermined public confidence in the integrity of the judicial process.

Count 2 — Violation of Canon 3B(2) — Failure to be Faithful to the Law and Maintain Professional Competence in It

Canon 3B(2): "A judge shall be faithful to the law and shall maintain professional competence in it. A judge shall not be swayed by partisan interests, public clamor, or fear of criticism."

Elements Alleged

The presiding judicial officer(s) failed to apply United States v. Cronic, 466 U.S. 648 (1984), and the line of authority requiring a court to inquire when defense counsel's failure to subject the prosecution's case to meaningful adversarial testing gives rise to a presumption of prejudice. Failure to conduct or record such an inquiry over a course of continued incarceration is a departure from professional competence in the applicable law.

Count 3 — Violation of Canon 3B(5) — Failure to Perform Judicial Duties Without Bias or Prejudice

Canon 3B(5): "A judge shall perform judicial duties without bias or prejudice."

Elements Alleged

Sustained inaction in the face of a documented complaining-witness recantation and a total defense-motion vacuum implicates the appearance, and potentially the substance, of judicial bias in favor of the prosecution and against the pretrial defendant. Complainant respectfully requests the Commission investigate whether the pattern of inaction was the product of bias or prejudice within the meaning of Canon 3B(5).

Count 4 — Violation of Canon 3B(8) — Failure to Accord Full Right to Be Heard

Canon 3B(8): "A judge shall accord to every person who has a legal interest in a proceeding, or that person's lawyer, the right to be heard according to law."

Elements Alleged

Because Kyle Scott Harris's court-appointed counsel filed no substantive pretrial motion, and because the presiding judicial officer(s) did not inquire, appoint substitute counsel, or otherwise create a mechanism by which the pretrial defendant could be heard on bond, discovery, suppression, dismissal, or the recantation of the complaining witness, Kyle Scott Harris was effectively denied the right to be heard on any pretrial matter of consequence during his continuing detention.

Count 5 — Violation of Canon 3C(1) — Failure to Diligently Discharge Administrative Responsibilities

Canon 3C(1): "A judge shall diligently and promptly discharge the judge's administrative responsibilities without bias or prejudice and maintain professional competence in judicial administration, and should cooperate with other judges and court officials in the administration of court business."

Elements Alleged

Docket management is a core administrative responsibility of the presiding judge. A criminal case in which a defendant sits in continuous pretrial detention while court-appointed counsel files nothing over an extended period reflects an administrative failure of docket supervision inconsistent with Canon 3C(1).

Count 6 — Violation of Canon 3D(2) — Failure to Take Appropriate Action Regarding Lawyer Misconduct

Canon 3D(2): "A judge who receives information clearly establishing that a lawyer has committed a violation of the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct should take appropriate action. A judge having knowledge that a lawyer has committed a violation of the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct that raises a substantial question as to the lawyer's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness as a lawyer in other respects shall inform the State Bar's Office of the Chief Disciplinary Counsel."

Elements Alleged

The total non-filing of substantive pretrial motions in a case involving a continuously incarcerated defendant and a documented complaining-witness recantation raises a substantial question as to the fitness of the lawyer(s) to practice law under Rule 1.01 (Competent and Diligent Representation), Rule 1.03 (Communication), and Rule 3.02 (Minimizing the Burdens of Litigation) of the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct. Upon information and belief the presiding judicial officer(s) did not inform the State Bar of Texas of this conduct as required by Canon 3D(2).

Investigation Requested

  • Identify from Commission and court records the presiding judicial officer(s) in Cause No. D-1-DC-25-303689 (Travis County) and any related pretrial matters against Kyle Scott Harris in Travis County and Collin County.
  • Obtain from the applicable district clerks the complete docket sheet, calendar of settings and hearings, and any transcripts or audio recordings of pretrial appearances during the period of Kyle Scott Harris's continuous pretrial detention.
  • Determine whether the presiding judicial officer(s) conducted any on-the-record inquiry into the effectiveness of appointed counsel or the absence of substantive pretrial filings.
  • Determine whether the presiding judicial officer(s) received actual notice of the recantation by Bobbi Jo Rice and, if so, what action if any was taken.
  • Determine whether the presiding judicial officer(s) reported the conduct of Attorney Holub or Attorney Brad [surname to confirm] to the State Bar of Texas Office of the Chief Disciplinary Counsel as required by Canon 3D(2).
  • Coordinate as appropriate with the State Bar of Texas Office of the Chief Disciplinary Counsel, which has received contemporaneous grievances against both attorneys of record.
  • Coordinate as appropriate with the Melissa Police Department, the Collin County Sheriff's Office, and the Texas Department of State Health Services Zoonosis Control Branch, each of which has received contemporaneous filings by Complainant relating to the underlying facts.
  • Take such further action as the Commission deems appropriate under Chapter 33 of the Texas Government Code and the Texas Constitution.

Kyle Scott Harris, as an indigent pretrial detainee, is limited in his ability to research and file his own grievance; complainant files this grievance in aid of Kyle Scott Harris's Sixth Amendment right to the effective assistance of counsel and Texas constitutional right to competent representation.

Summary of Grievance

Respondent attorney Christopher Willia Holub has served as court-appointed counsel to Kyle Scott Harris in three active Travis County criminal cause numbers — D-1-DC-25-303689 (Assault Family / Household Member — Impede Breath / Circulation, Third Degree Felony), C-1-CR-25-502783 (Terroristic Threat, Class A Misdemeanor), and C-1-CR-25-502784 (Unlawful Restraint, Class A Misdemeanor). Public docket examination in each cause number shows that respondent has drafted, filed, and set for hearing zero of the twelve standard pretrial defense motions catalogued in the attached Twelve-Motion Gap Audit (Exhibit A) — motions which would be non-discretionary in any competent Texas Assault Family Violence — Impede prosecution defense.

The unfiled motions include, without limitation: a Michael Morton Act discovery demand (Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 39.14); a Brady/Giglio exculpatory-and-impeachment disclosure demand; a bond reduction motion (Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Art. 17.15); a motion to suppress statements under Miranda and Article 38.22; a motion in limine on Rule 404(b) extraneous offenses; a motion for expert-witness funds under Ake v. Oklahoma, 470 U.S. 68 (1985); a motion for grand jury transcripts; a motion to compel outcry-witness disclosure under Article 38.072; a motion for defensive-issues character evidence under Rule 404(a)(2); a Sixth Amendment speedy-trial demand; a motion to sever joined offenses under Tex. Penal § 3.04; and a motion to preserve evidence and compel chain-of-custody over the exculpatory Short Message Service [SMS] recantation thread from complaining witness Bobbi Jo to third-party witness Beth Martin.

The failure is uniform, sustained, and unexplained by any strategic rationale visible on the record. It has caused specific, ongoing prejudice to Kyle Scott Harris, an indigent pretrial detainee, and violates Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct 1.01, 1.03, and 1.04.

Factual Basis

Fact 1 — Appointment

Respondent Christopher Willia Holub was appointed by a Travis County court to represent Kyle Scott Harris in cause numbers D-1-DC-25-303689, C-1-CR-25-502783, and C-1-CR-25-502784. Kyle Scott Harris is indigent and has no other counsel of record in those matters.

Fact 2 — Continuous Custody

Kyle Scott Harris has been continuously held in pretrial custody at the Travis County Correctional Complex, 3614 Bill Price Road, Del Valle, Texas 78617, without release, without a bond-reduction hearing being set, and without a personal-recognizance motion being filed.

Fact 3 — Exculpatory Recantation Known to Counsel

Complaining witness Bobbi Jo has, since the initial charging decision, communicated in writing that the underlying event as charged did not occur. Bobbi Jo stated verbatim to a witness who has since relayed the statement: "I sent an email to the District Attorney stating that this never happened." The recantation exists in Short Message Service [SMS] format between Bobbi Jo and third-party witness Beth Martin, and in electronic-mail format between Bobbi Jo and the Travis County District Attorney's Office. Kyle Scott Harris has communicated the existence of this exculpatory material to respondent by telephone from custody. Respondent has neither filed a written Michael Morton Act demand nor a written Brady demand seeking production of this material.

Fact 4 — Twelve-For-Twelve Motion Gap

Public docket examination in all three cause numbers as of the date of this filing reveals zero (0) of the twelve standard pretrial motions catalogued in the attached Twelve-Motion Gap Audit filed by respondent. See Exhibit A. Each of the twelve motions is a standard, expected filing in any competent Texas Assault Family Violence — Impede prosecution defense.

Fact 5 — No Communicated Strategic Rationale

Kyle Scott Harris has communicated to complainant that respondent has not explained any strategic rationale for declining to file any of the twelve motions. No client-informed-consent-to-strategic-inaction discussion has occurred on any of the twelve motions. Respondent has not returned repeated telephone requests for case-status updates from Kyle Scott Harris.

Fact 6 — Prejudice

The absence of a Michael Morton Act demand has kept the Bobbi Jo recantation electronic-mail off the record. The absence of a preservation motion has left the exculpatory Short Message Service [SMS] thread vulnerable to destruction without evidence-tampering exposure attaching to any custodian. The absence of a bond-reduction motion has kept Kyle Scott Harris in custody, unable to participate meaningfully in his own defense, unable to contact witnesses, and unable to develop mitigation. Each is a discrete, ongoing prejudice.

Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct — Violations Alleged

Rule 1.01 — Competent and Diligent Representation
"A lawyer shall not accept or continue employment in a legal matter which the lawyer knows or should know is beyond the lawyer's competence, without association of a lawyer who is competent to handle it. … In representing a client, a lawyer shall not: (1) neglect a legal matter entrusted to the lawyer; or (2) frequently fail to carry out completely the obligations that the lawyer owes to a client or clients."

Application: Filing zero of twelve standard pretrial motions across three cause numbers over a sustained period is neglect within the meaning of Rule 1.01(b)(1). It is also a frequent failure to carry out client obligations within the meaning of Rule 1.01(b)(2). It reflects either lack of competence or a decision to accept representation the respondent should have declined or associated additional counsel to handle.

Rule 1.03 — Communication
"(a) A lawyer shall keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and promptly comply with reasonable requests for information. (b) A lawyer shall explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation."

Application: Respondent has not communicated any strategic rationale for the twelve-for-twelve motion gap. Respondent has not returned repeated telephone-message inquiries from Kyle Scott Harris. Respondent has not explained the significance of the Bobbi Jo recantation, has not explained the discovery vehicles available under Article 39.14, and has not explained the bond-reduction posture. Rule 1.03(a) and (b) are both implicated.

Rule 1.04 — Fees / Diligence — read with Preamble ¶ 4 (zeal within the bounds of the law)
Texas Preamble to the Disciplinary Rules recognizes that a lawyer should act with commitment and dedication to the interests of the client and with zeal in advocacy upon the client's behalf.

Application: The uniform, unexplained twelve-for-twelve gap is not zealous advocacy within the bounds of the law. It is the opposite — absence of advocacy on the pretrial record where advocacy is expected, permitted, and materially favorable to the client.

Constitutional Overlay — Sixth Amendment Ineffective Assistance of Counsel

Respondent's conduct also independently supports a post-conviction claim of ineffective assistance of counsel under Strickland v. Washington, 466 U.S. 668 (1984). The State Bar disciplinary standard and the Sixth Amendment standard are not identical, but the record supporting one substantially overlaps the record supporting the other. The State Bar of Texas is asked to consider this grievance on its own disciplinary merits without regard to any pending or contemplated Sixth Amendment litigation.

Relief Sought

Complainant respectfully requests that the Office of the Chief Disciplinary Counsel:

  1. Classify this grievance as a Complaint (not merely an Inquiry) upon initial review, given the Twelve-Motion Gap Audit attached as Exhibit A.
  2. Open a formal investigation into respondent Christopher Willia Holub's representation of Kyle Scott Harris in cause numbers D-1-DC-25-303689, C-1-CR-25-502783, and C-1-CR-25-502784.
  3. Compel respondent to produce his written case file, calendar entries, drafted-but-unfiled motions (if any), and correspondence with Kyle Scott Harris and the Travis County District Attorney's Office.
  4. Refer this grievance to the appropriate Grievance Committee for evidentiary panel proceedings if the investigation confirms the twelve-for-twelve gap.
  5. Notify complainant in writing of the classification decision, investigative status, and disposition, at the mailing address above.
  6. Consider, in the interest of Kyle Scott Harris as an indigent pretrial detainee, expedited handling given the ongoing custodial prejudice.

Rule 1.03 — Communication
"(a) A lawyer shall keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and promptly comply with reasonable requests for information. (b) A lawyer shall explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation."

Application: Respondent has not communicated any strategic rationale for the twelve-for-twelve motion gap. Respondent has not returned repeated telephone-message inquiries from Kyle Scott Harris. Respondent has not explained the significance of the Bobbi Jo recantation, the discovery vehicles available under Article 39.14, or the bond-reduction posture. Rule 1.03(a) and (b) are both implicated.

Rule 1.04 — Fees / Diligence — read with Preamble ¶ 4 (zeal within the bounds of the law)
Texas Preamble to the Disciplinary Rules recognizes that a lawyer should act with commitment and dedication to the interests of the client and with zeal in advocacy upon the client's behalf.

Application: A uniform, unexplained twelve-for-twelve gap across four cause numbers is not zealous advocacy — it is absence of advocacy on the pretrial record.

Constitutional Overlay — Sixth Amendment Ineffective Assistance of Counsel

Respondent's conduct also independently supports a post-conviction claim of ineffective assistance of counsel under Strickland v. Washington, 466 U.S. 668 (1984). The State Bar disciplinary standard and the Sixth Amendment standard are not identical, but the record supporting one substantially overlaps the record supporting the other. The State Bar of Texas is asked to consider this grievance on its own disciplinary merits without regard to any pending or contemplated Sixth Amendment litigation.

Relief Sought

Complainant respectfully requests that the Office of the Chief Disciplinary Counsel:

  1. Classify this grievance as a Complaint (not merely an Inquiry) upon initial review, given the Twelve-Motion Gap Audit attached as Exhibit A.
  2. Open a formal investigation into respondent John B. "Brad"'s representation of Kyle Scott Harris in cause numbers 199-80678-2026, 199-80977-2026, 429-55152-2025, and 49928-2025.
  3. Compel respondent to produce his written case file, calendar entries, drafted-but-unfiled motions (if any), and correspondence with Kyle Scott Harris and the Collin County District Attorney's Office.
  4. Refer this grievance to the appropriate Grievance Committee for evidentiary panel proceedings if the investigation confirms the twelve-for-twelve gap across four cause numbers.
  5. Notify complainant in writing of the classification decision, investigative status, and disposition.
  6. Consider, in the interest of Kyle Scott Harris as an indigent pretrial detainee, expedited handling given the ongoing custodial prejudice.

Federal Statutory Framework

18 U.S.C. § 242 — Deprivation of Rights Under Color of Law
Whoever, under color of any law, statute, ordinance, regulation, or custom, willfully subjects any person to the deprivation of any rights, privileges, or immunities secured or protected by the Constitution or laws of the United States, shall be subject to federal criminal penalty. Enhanced penalties apply where bodily injury results, or where the deprivation includes kidnapping, aggravated sexual abuse, or an attempt to kill.
18 U.S.C. § 241 — Conspiracy Against Rights
If two or more persons conspire to injure, oppress, threaten, or intimidate any person in any State in the free exercise or enjoyment of any right or privilege secured to him by the Constitution or laws of the United States, they shall be subject to federal criminal penalty.

Summary of Basis

Section 1 — Who to Contact, by Title (call in this order)

OrderTitleWhy
1 Public Information Officer / Records Custodian Legally required point of contact for all Chapter 552 requests. Every Texas governmental body must designate one. Start here so nothing is deemed "not received."
2 Shelter Director / Animal Services Manager Custodian of intake, disposition, and euthanasia decision records. Signs off on euthanasia.
3 Veterinarian on Staff / Contract Veterinarian Signs euthanasia forms and medical records; can confirm chip-scan protocol was followed.

7 Collin County Commissioners Court — County Judge's office Escalation channel if the shelter stonewalls or misses the ten-business-day Texas Public Information Act deadline.

Do not ask for "the manager" — ask by title. If a receptionist deflects, say: "I am requesting the name and email of the designated Public Information Officer for Collin County Animal Services under Texas Government Code § 552.204."

Section 2 — Records to Request (exact list)

For every record listed below, cite the Texas Public Information Act request number and the governing statute. Request electronic delivery as PDF with metadata intact.

2A · Intake Records

  1. Intake ticket or animal-in-custody form for the animal named "Nebula" (or matching description) surrendered or impounded between [date range — to confirm with Kyle Scott Harris: earliest suspected date through today].
  2. Surrender form signed by the person delivering the animal (owner-surrender vs. stray impoundment vs. protective-custody).
  3. Photograph(s) taken at intake.
  4. Description form: breed, weight, sex, color, age estimate, distinguishing marks.
  5. Microchip scan record — chip found (yes / no), chip number if scanned, registry lookup result.

2B · Custody Chain Records

  1. Kennel assignment log — every kennel change, date, staff initials.
  2. Daily observation notes (kennel cards).
  3. Visitor log — every person who requested to see this animal, redeem this animal, or claim ownership.
  4. All incoming phone calls or electronic mail referencing this animal by name, chip, or description.
  5. Any HOLD placed on the animal (protective custody, evidence, quarantine).

2C · Disposition Records — MOST IMPORTANT

  1. Disposition form or outcome record — adopted / returned to owner / transferred / euthanized / died in care / escaped.
  2. If euthanized: euthanasia authorization form, name and license number of the veterinarian who signed, drug used, dosage, date, time, staff witness.

2D · Compliance Records

  1. All Chapter 823 stray-holding-period documentation (Texas requires a minimum 72-hour hold for strays before disposition).
  2. All communications between Collin County Animal Services and any law-enforcement agency regarding this animal.
  3. All communications between Collin County Animal Services and Bobbi Jo Rice, Todd Boatwright, or any third party regarding this animal.

Section 5 — Parallel Pursuit (do not wait on the shelter alone)

5A · Microchip Registry Lookup (independent chain of custody)

  • If Nebula was chipped, look up the chip on the American Animal Hospital Association Universal Microchip Lookup: petmicrochiplookup.org.
  • This returns the registry (HomeAgain, 24PetWatch, American Kennel Club Reunite, Michelson Found Animals, and similar).
  • Contact the registry directly. Registries keep a log of every "found pet" ping against the chip number, including which shelter scanned it, what date, what time. This is independent of the shelter's own records and is an excellent cross-check.

5B · Collin County Sheriff's Office — Animal Cruelty Investigator

  • Non-emergency line: (972) 547-5100.
  • File a report titled: "Suspected violation of Texas Penal Code § 42.092 (Cruelty to Non-Livestock Animals) and § 32.45 (Misapplication of Fiduciary Property) — canine surrendered to shelter by non-owner."

5C · Collin County District Attorney

  • District Attorney Greg Willis.

Section 6 — What Not to Say or Do (landmines)

  • Do not threaten litigation on the first call. It triggers "route everything to the County Attorney" and slows records production by weeks.
  • Do not send electronic mail from a personal Gmail address. Use troy@drrealty.us — professional posture matters.
  • Do not accept a verbal "she's not here" without a written "no responsive records" statement. Verbal denials are unenforceable.
  • Do not let the phone call end without a case or intake number.
  • Do not send the Texas Public Information Act request only by electronic mail. Certified mail plus electronic mail plus facsimile creates a bulletproof service record.
  • Do not identify Kyle Scott Harris by inmate number in the first contact — it leads to bias. Introduce Kyle as "the registered owner" first; identify his incarceration only if directly relevant.
  • Do not ask "did you euthanize Nebula?" — instead ask "please produce the disposition record for the animal identified above." Neutral, procedural, unemotional.

Section 7 — Timeline and Service-Level Agreement

DayAction
Day 0 (today) Phone call to Collin County Animal Services · Texas Public Information Act letter sent certified mail plus electronic mail plus facsimile · Microchip registry query · Sheriff report filed.
Day 1 Written acknowledgment of Texas Public Information Act receipt (demand it) · Confirm HOLD placed.
Day 3 First follow-up if no acknowledgment.
Day 10 (business) Texas Public Information Act statutory production deadline · If withheld, they must have requested an Attorney General opinion.
Day 11+ If missed: file complaint with the Texas Attorney General under Texas Government Code § 552.321 for mandamus.

Section 8 — Open Intake from Kyle (needed to fully load the request)

  • Nebula's microchip number (if chipped).
  • Nebula's breed, color, sex, weight, age.
  • Approximate date Bobbi Jo Rice removed Nebula from Kyle Scott Harris's custody.
  • Any prior veterinarian who has records on Nebula.
  • Kyle Scott Harris's photos of Nebula (proof of ownership).
  • Any prior communication (text message or electronic mail) where Bobbi Jo Rice acknowledged Nebula belongs to Kyle Scott Harris.
  • Name of anyone Kyle Scott Harris asked to check on Nebula, and their finding.
